review: Settled as written: a prayer. ਜਗਜੀਵਨ has no aunkar and stands among the vocatives of the line before (ਸੁਰਿ ਨਰ ਨਾਥ … ਅਪਾਰਾ), with the imperative ਕਰਹੁ after it; a vocative cannot be the subject of the third-person ਮਿਲੇ, so its subject is Nanak, optative (Darpan: ਹੇ ਜਗਤ ਦੇ ਜੀਵਨ! … ਅਡੋਲਤਾ ਵਿਚ ਨਿਵਾਸ ਮਿਲੇ; Faridkot also reads ਹੇ ਜਗ ਜੀਵਨ). In Asa 436.1 no address surrounds the half-line and the second half (ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਬੂਝ ਬੁਝਾਈਐ) is a third-person statement, so ਜਗਜੀਵਨ is the One met (Darpan glosses it the Lord, not a vocative): its statement stands. The two differ by their grammar; neither changes.

Settled as written: 10.1's rendering kept except where this text differs (heading; ਹਉ already rendered I; last line without ਜਨ, so ਮਿਲਿ is meeting the Sat Sangat, as the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka read it here). The Naam gloss is rightly dropped: the Naam is unglossed from 489.1 on in this raag. Line 6 (en) keeps the writer's rewording: 10.1's own line 5 shares a 13-word run with Sant Singh Khalsa (have faith in the Lord, Har, Har, and a thirst for the Lord), which fails the copy rule; live 10.1 line 5 (en) is to take this batch's wording, so the two stay identical.
reviewer_fix: no change in this batch; live 10.1 en line 5 → Great, very great, is the fortune of the Lord's servants who hold faith in the Lord, Har Har, and who thirst for the Lord.

issue: Line 8: ਤ੍ਰਿਭਵਣ ਸੋਝੀ ਪਾਇ: understanding of the three worlds, or of the Lord who pervades the three worlds.
our reading: Kept: gains understanding of the three worlds.
alternatives: The Darpan glosses ਤ੍ਰਿਭਵਣ as the Lord pervading the three worlds (ਤਿੰਨ ਭਵਨਾਂ ਵਿਚ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ).
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka reads the three worlds themselves (ਤੀਨੋਂ ਲੋਕੋਂ ਕੀ ਸੁਧ; ਤ੍ਰਿਲੋਕੀ ਕੀ ਸਮਝ), which is the line's plain wording; the Darpan's sense is not excluded by it.

issue: Copy rule: overlap.py finds one 10-word run against the Darpan (pa) in lines 0-1: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੂ ਦੀ ਕਿਰਪਾ ਨਾਲ ਮਿਲਦਾ ਹੈ + ਰਾਗ ਗੂਜਰੀ, ਘਰ ... ਵਿੱਚ.
our reading: Kept: both pieces are the fixed house formulas for ੴ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ and for a heading, word for word as in every earlier raag (348.2, 366.1, 439.1 and the rest).
alternatives: Reword the formula or the heading for this verse alone.
decided because: The run only spans two set formulas joined across a line break, not a rendering of the verse; changing them here would break the consistency rule. All verse lines have 0 runs of 10+ against every copied source (pa and en).

issue: ਸਾਰੇ: a verb (takes care of, keeps in mind) or the adjective all (ਸਭ ਸਥਾਨੋਂ ਮੇਂ ਜੀਵੋਂ ਕੀ, the Faridkot Teeka).
our reading: He ever looks after (us) and takes care (of us): ਸਾਰੇ a verb beside ਸੰਮ੍ਹਾਲੇ.
alternatives: He ever takes care of all (Faridkot Teeka).
decided because: The Darpan's grammar (ਸਾਰੇ, ਸਾਰ ਲੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ) and the paired verbs; Manmohan Singh reads it the same way.

issue: Who recites the Vedas (ਪੜਹਿ, plural)?
our reading: Brahma: ਉਪਜੇ and ਪੜਹਿ are both honorific plurals for him (the Faridkot Teeka; Sant Singh Khalsa).
alternatives: The pandits recite the Vedas Brahma composed (the Darpan); people recite them (Manmohan Singh).
decided because: Both verbs of the line share one subject, and the next line (ਤਾ ਕੋ ਅੰਤੁ … ਆਵਤ ਜਾਤ ਰਹੈ) continues Brahma's story.

issue: The order of the two clauses: does the Light awaken and then the Guru settle the strife, or the reverse?
our reading: When the True Guru settles the strife, the Light within and the Shabad's melody awaken.
alternatives: In one in whom the Light is within and the Shabad awakens, the True Guru settles the strife (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: The Darpan reads the Guru's settling as the cause; the line answers the Siddhas' strife in the line before.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਸਹਜਿ ਮਿਲੇ ਜਗਜੀਵਨ: a statement (Nanak meets / the Life of the world is met in Sahaj) or a petition.
our reading: A petition: may Nanak meet (you) in Sahaj, O Life of the world; it is followed by the command ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰਹੁ.
alternatives: Nanak merges in Sahaj into the Life of the world (Sant Singh Khalsa); O Life of the world, you are met in Sahaj (Faridkot). Our 436.1 renders the same half-line as a statement: O Nanak, the Life of the world is met in Sahaj.
decided because: The Darpan reads a prayer here, and the line's second half is a request; reviewers may wish to compare with 436.1, where no request follows.

issue: Ji / Jiu at the end of lines 1 to 4.
our reading: An address to the listener, rendered O brother in lines 1 and 3, the sentence's opening lines; left unrendered in lines 2 and 4, which continue the same address; explained in one note.
alternatives: A word of reverence for God (as our 10.3 note reads it in So Purakh).
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਜੀ here as ਹੇ ਭਾਈ, and the shabad speaks to the listener (ਤੁਮ ਸੇਵਾ ਕਰਹੁ).

issue: ਗੁਰ ਤੇ ਗੁਰੁ ਹੋਇਆ: whom it tells of.
our reading: Through the Guru (the disciple) has become the Guru; the two readings in a note.
alternatives: The Guru's own experience, Guru Amar Das from Guru Angad (Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya; Manmohan Singh names Lahna); anyone who takes the Guru's refuge becomes like the Guru (the Darpan).
decided because: The line itself names no one; the bracket keeps both readings open and the note names them.

issue: ਜਿਸ ਕਾ ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ ਗਵਾਏ: who removes the pride?
our reading: The Lord (in brackets).
alternatives: The person himself sheds his ego (Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka and Manmohan Singh: the Lord; ਜਿਸ ਕਾ (whose) makes the person the possessor, not the doer.

issue: ਨਾ ਕਾਸੀ ਮਤਿ ਜਾਇ: how wisdom is not lost.
our reading: Nor is wisdom lost (by staying away from) Kashi.
alternatives: By living at Kashi a base mind is not destroyed (the Faridkot Teeka); wisdom is not lost in Banaras (Sant Singh Khalsa, literal).
decided because: The Darpan: the pilgrimage neither gives wisdom nor, left undone, takes it away; the bracket keeps the line's parallel.

issue: ਪੰਚ ਭੂ ਆਤਮਾ.
our reading: The self made of the five elements, the mind; the Darpan's reading in a note.
alternatives: The mind under the sway of the five, lust and the rest (the Darpan); the soul overcoming the five elements (Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: Bhai Vir Singh's Santhya (ਪੰਚ ਭੂ ਆਤਮਨ, the inner faculty made of the five elements, with ਇਹੁ ਮਨੁ ਪੰਚ ਤਤ ਤੇ ਜਨਮਾ as proof) and the Faridkot Teeka agree; ਵਸਿ ਕਰਹਿ has the self as its object.

issue: This shabad is repeated from Rehras (10.1).
our reading: Its meanings are taken from 10.1, with its own two heading lines; the last line follows this text (ਮਿਲਿ ਨਾਨਕ, without ਜਨ: O Nanak, meeting in it …); the inline Naam gloss of 10.1 is dropped, as Gujri leaves the Naam unglossed; the English of line 6 is reworded (who hold faith … and who thirst for the Lord), since 10.1's wording shares a 13-word run with Sant Singh Khalsa.
alternatives: Keep 10.1's English of line 6 unchanged.
decided because: The copy rule; reviewers may wish to apply the same rewording to 10.1.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਜਨ: servant Nanak or the Lord's servants (plural).
our reading: Servant Nanak is in the Lord's refuge.
alternatives: O Nanak, the Lord's servants stay in his refuge (the Darpan).
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka (ਮੈਂ ਦਾਸ ਨੇ … ਤੇਰੀ ਸਰਣ ਲਈ ਹੈ) and the prayer of the line before (ਹੋਹੁ ਜਨ ਊਪਰਿ) for the one servant.

issue: ਸਤਸੰਗਤਿ ਗੁਰ ਕੀ ਹਰਿ ਪਿਆਰੀ ਜਿਨ …: dear to whom?
our reading: Dear to the Lord is the Guru's Sat Sangat, (the company) of those to whose minds the Name is sweet.
alternatives: The Sat Sangat is dear to those to whom the Name is sweet (the Darpan, leaving ਹਰਿ unread).
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka; it accounts for ਹਰਿ before ਪਿਆਰੀ.

issue: Line 5: ਜਪ ਤਪ ਸੰਜਮ ਕਰਮ ਧਰਮ ਹਰਿ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਜਨਿ ਗਾਇਓ: Kirtan in place of the rites, or Kirtan as the rites.
our reading: Kept: in place of repetition, austerity, self-restraint, rites and dharma, the servant has sung the Lord's Kirtan.
alternatives: The Darpan and both English translations: for the servant, Kirtan is itself his japa, tapa, sanjam and rites.
decided because: Faridkot reads ਸਭ ਕੇ ਸਥਾਨ (in place of all these), and the two readings come to the same sense; the line names no copula, so neither is wrong.

issue: Line 8: ਹਾਥਿ ਚਰਿਓ ਹਰਿ ਥੋਕਾ: ਥੋਕਾ as the whole store (ਭੰਡਾਰ) or as a precious thing.
our reading: Kept: the Lord, the whole store, has come into my hands.
alternatives: The Darpan: ਥੋਕ, ਪਦਾਰਥ (the most precious thing); Faridkot: ਬੜਾ ਪਦਾਰਥ; the English translations: the real substance.
decided because: ਥੋਕ is a mass, a whole lot; the store and the great substance both name the Lord as the wealth gained, so the sense is not changed.

issue: ਜਿਨ (plural) and ਜਿਨਿ (singular) in one line; who is to instruct the speaker.
our reading: Of those who have found the True Guru, may one who has found the Lord God instruct me and make the Lord sweet (a wish, with the Rahao's ਕੋਈ ਆਇ ਮਿਲੈ).
alternatives: Faridkot and the English translations: whoever has found the Lord through the True Guru has made the Lord sweet to me (a statement in the past); the Darpan: two groups, those who have seen the Guru and the one who has found God.
decided because: ਲਗਾਵੈ is subjunctive and the Rahao is a longing for someone to come; the plural ਜਿਨ and singular ਜਿਨਿ are both kept.

issue: Whose mind and body are cooled.
our reading: The fortunate one who meditates on the Name (third person, ਧਿਆਵੈ).
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa and Manmohan Singh: my mind and body.
decided because: ਧਿਆਵੈ is third person singular; the Darpan and Faridkot read it so.

issue: The shabad repeats 10.2 (Sodar), whose line reads ਮਿਲੇ ਸੁ ਤਰਿਆ; here the Granth has ਮਿਲੇ ਸਿ ਤਰਿਆ.
our reading: Plural: those who have joined the Sat Sangat have crossed over; by the Guru's grace they have attained the supreme state. Every other line keeps 10.2's meaning word for word.
alternatives: Keep 10.2's singular (whoever has joined … he has attained).
decided because: ਸਿ is the plural of ਸੁ (the Darpan here: ਸਿ, ਉਹ ਬੰਦੇ); the meaning is the same, only the number follows this text.

issue: Who has wandered the world and now come to the Lord's door (ਆਏ).
our reading: (We) have roamed the whole world; now (we) have come to the Lord's door.
alternatives: The Darpan: the people who, after wandering, fall at God's door; the Santhya: those who came to Guru Ram Das.
decided because: ਆਏ with no named subject reads naturally as the speaker's own we, as Faridkot (ਹਮ) and both English translations take it; the closing line's ਤਾਰੀ agrees.

issue: ਧੋਖਾ: worry or doubt.
our reading: doubt (ਸੰਸਾ).
alternatives: The Darpan: ਫ਼ਿਕਰ, worry.
decided because: Faridkot, the Santhya (ਸੰਸੇ ਬ੍ਰਿਤੀ, ਭੁਲਾਵਾ) and Manmohan Singh read doubt, and the line's first half already names the anxiety (ਚਿੰਤ).

issue: ਇਹੁ ਮਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਰੰਗਿ ਰੰਗੇ: a statement or a command.
our reading: Statement: this mind is dyed in the Lord's love.
alternatives: The Darpan: ਰੰਗੇ = ਰੰਗਿ, dye your mind in the Lord's love (a command).
decided because: Faridkot, the Santhya and both English translations read it as done; the shabad tells what the son has brought home.

issue: What the stubborn renunciant condemned and gave up and then eats again and again.
our reading: Kept as the words say: what was not to be condemned he condemned and gave up, and that very thing he eats again and again.
alternatives: The Darpan: household life, whose food he still takes from householders; Faridkot: the household goods the shastras do not condemn, or what the saints renounced; the English translations: the food the blameless have discarded.
decided because: The words name no object; the plain reading fits every commentary's sense without choosing among them.

issue: ਪਰਵਾਣੁ ਗਿਰਸਤ ਉਦਾਸ: the householder who stays detached, or either the householder or the renunciant.
our reading: Whether householder or renunciant, the one who has met the Perfect Guru is accepted.
alternatives: The Darpan: living as a householder, detached from Maya, he is accepted.
decided because: Faridkot and both English translations read the two words as two states; the shabad's point is that neither worldly cleverness nor proud renunciation counts, only meeting the Guru.

issue: ਪਾਇਅਉ: first person or third.
our reading: Third person, following the Rahao's ਗਾਇਓ: the one who sang the Lord's praise found the peace above all peace.
alternatives: A first-person reading (I found).
decided because: The Darpan, Faridkot and both English translations read the third person.

issue: ਰੰਗਿ ਰਵਿਓ ਰੰਗਿ ਰਾਤਾ: of God or of the devotee.
our reading: God dwells in every body; the servant delights in him with love, dyed in his love.
alternatives: Faridkot: the one whose joy pervades all, in his love the Gurmukh is dyed; the English translations: I am immersed in his love.
decided because: The Darpan's reading, which the stanza's subject (the one who knows no other) carries on from line 7.

issue: ਨਾਮੁ ਸੁਖ ਰਾਜਾ.
our reading: The Naam is the king of comforts (the Darpan's ਸੁਖਾਂ ਦਾ ਰਾਜਾ).
alternatives: Faridkot: the Naam is comfort, the Naam is king; Manmohan Singh: royal peace.
decided because: ਸੁਖ ਰਾਜਾ read as one compound, as each other item of the line is a single noun phrase after ਨਾਮੁ.

issue: ਬਿਨਸਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ ਜਾਈ: of the Naam or of the person.
our reading: Of the person: (one) neither perishes nor comes and goes.
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa and Manmohan Singh: the treasure of the Naam neither dies nor goes anywhere.
decided because: ਆਵੈ ਜਾਈ is coming and going in births; the Darpan and Faridkot read it of the one in whom the Guru set the Naam.

issue: ਸਗਲ ਸ੍ਰਿਸਟਿ ਕੋ ਧਣੀ ਕਹੀਜੈ: who is called the master of creation.
our reading: God is called the Master of the whole creation, yet takes the servant's side beyond compare.
alternatives: The Darpan: by the Name the servant comes to be called the master of the world.
decided because: Faridkot and both translations read God; the Rahao addresses the Thakur and his Name.

issue: ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ ਨਾਨਕ ਬੁਧਿ ਪਾਈ: Nanak as subject or addressed.
our reading: Nanak has gained understanding in the Saadh Sangat (style.md §12: Nanak speaks of himself).
alternatives: The Darpan: O Nanak, whoever gains understanding in the Saadh Sangat has the Lord's praise as support.
decided because: No other subject is named; Manmohan Singh and Sant Singh Khalsa read Nanak as subject.

issue: ਪਿਆਰੋ: object (the Beloved Lord) or vocative (O dear ones).
our reading: Object: worship the Beloved day and night.
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa and Manmohan Singh: vocative, O my dear.
decided because: The Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ gives ਪਿਆਰੇ (ਹਰੀ) ਨੂੰ and the Faridkot Teeka reads ਮੋਹਨ ਪਿਆਰੇ ਕੋ; ਆਰਾਧਹੁ needs an object, and the Rahao names the Beloved (ਮੋਹਨੁ).

issue: ਮਿਲਿ ਵਰ ਨਾਰੀ: who sings.
our reading: Meeting the Husband (Lord), the brides (souls) have sung songs of joy.
alternatives: Darpan: the women are the senses (ਗਿਆਨ-ਇੰਦ੍ਰੇ) that, meeting the Husband, sing; Faridkot: meeting the excellent devotees (ਵਰ = excellent, ਨਾਰੀ = devotees), the servants sang.
decided because: ਨਾਰੀ is plural (Darpan: ਨਾਰੀਆਂ ਨੇ) and ਵਰ the Husband-Lord, the plain bride imagery of Gurbani; the senses reading is a further gloss the line does not state.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ: subject or vocative.
our reading: Nanak has come to lean on the Creator and has cast off other hopes.
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, (the one in whose heart) the Creator's support has come has cast off other hopes.
decided because: The whole shabad is Nanak's own prayer in the first person; Nanak speaks of himself (style.md §12), no other subject is named.

issue: ਗੁਰ ਨਾਨਕ: Guru Nanak as the one who laid the foundation, or the Guru, with Nanak the signature.
our reading: The Guru has laid an unshakeable foundation, O Nanak, which rises higher day by day.
alternatives: Santhya and Faridkot Teeka: Guru Nanak (Dev Ji) laid the foundation (of the Sikh faith); Sant Singh Khalsa likewise.
decided because: style.md §12: ਨਾਨਕ in the last line is the signature, never rendered Guru Nanak; ਗੁਰ goes with the words around it (ਨੀਵ ਧਰੀ ਗੁਰ, the Guru laid). The Darpan reads it so.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਗੁਣ ਸਦਾ ਬੀਚਾਰਿ: cause of the healing, or a further statement (we ever reflect).
our reading: Absolutive: the illness is gone, through ever dwelling on the Lord's virtues.
alternatives: Faridkot and Sant Singh Khalsa: and we ever reflect on the Lord's virtues.
decided because: ਬੀਚਾਰਿ with sihari is the conjunct participle (Darpan: ਮਨ ਵਿਚ ਟਿਕਾ ਕੇ; Santhya: ਗੁਣ ਗਾਉਣ ਨਾਲ).

issue: Who never set his mind on the Lord: I (the speaker), a third person (the Maya-bound mortal), or you.
our reading: First person: (I) never set my mind on the Lord; lines 1–4 a confession, lines 5–6 the plea.
alternatives: Darpan: the Maya-bound mortal (third person, habitual); Sant Singh Khalsa: you (second person).
decided because: The verbs are past (ਲਾਇਓ, ਬਿਹਾਨੀ, ਗਾਇਓ, ਧਾਇਓ, ਖਾਇਓ) and the second stanza asks the Lord not to count my deeds (ਗਨਹੁ ਨ ਮੋਹਿ ਕਮਾਇਓ); the Faridkot Teeka reads the first person throughout.

issue: ਗੋਬਿੰਦ: subject or vocative.
our reading: Gobind, in his mercy, has given (the devotees) the Guru's wisdom and a discerning intellect.
alternatives: Darpan: vocative, O Gobind, (those) to whom you have given.
decided because: ਦੀਆ is third person and no second-person word stands in the stanza; the simplest construction makes Gobind the giver.

issue: ਸਫਲ: of the Name (the fruit-bearing Name) or predicate of the deeds (they bear fruit).
our reading: Recitations, austerities and countless deeds find their fruit in remembering the Name.
alternatives: Darpan: all these are contained in remembering the Name that gives life its fruit (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh likewise).
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka reads ਸਫਲ as the predicate (ਨਾਮ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਸੇ ਸਫਲ ਹੋਤੀ ਹੈ), which needs no added verb; both say the Name fulfils them all.

issue: ਨ ਬਿਸਰੁ: addressed to God (may you never be forgotten) or to the listener (never forget).
our reading: Addressed to God: may I never forget you with a single breath, O Brahm, all-powerful God.
alternatives: Darpan: instruction to the listener, never forget all-powerful God.
decided because: ਬਿਸਰੁ is the imperative of ਬਿਸਰਨਾ (to be forgotten), as ਵਿਸਰੁ ਨਾਹੀ in Asa (378.2, rendered may I never forget you); the Faridkot Teeka reads it as a prayer.

issue: ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ ਜੋਗੁ: of the Lord (epithet) or of the Name (able to unite with the Cause of creation).
our reading: The Guru has given the Name of him who is the all-able Cause of creation.
alternatives: Darpan: the Name is able to unite one with the Root of creation.
decided because: The same words are an epithet of God in 502.2 (ਸ੍ਰੀਧਰ … ਕਰਣ ਕਾਰਣ ਜੋਗੁ); the Darpan's reading needs an added verb (ਮਿਲਾਣ).

issue: ਤ੍ਰਿਹਦਸ
our reading: the three (qualities of Maya) and the ten (senses), as the Darpan, the Shabdarth and the Faridkot Teeka gloss it
alternatives: read as one number, thirteen
decided because: all three commentaries split it into three gunas and ten senses (or ten thieves); the line names what the wealth is guarded from, which the five thieves of line 2 and these make plain

issue: ਸਹਜ ਭਾਇ ਜਾਇ ਤੇ ... ਜਾਗੇ: who or what goes
our reading: the tree of line 6 (the world, Maya) falls away with ease from those (ਤੇ) who stay awake in the Supreme Lord (Darpan, Santhya)
alternatives: Shabdarth: those who go (ਜਾਇ) into the state of Sahaj are awake; Sant Singh Khalsa: he alone reaches this tree; Faridkot: peace arises
decided because: ਜਾਇ is singular and ਜਾਗੇ plural, so ਜਾਇ has the tree (Maya) for subject and ਤੇ (they) goes with ਜਾਗੇ; two commentaries agree

issue: ਤਤੁ in ਪੁਹਪ ਪਤ੍ਰ ਤਤੁ ਡਾਲਾ
our reading: the Paarjat in the heart is the Lord, the Essence, whose flowers, leaves and branches are the world (Darpan)
alternatives: Shabdarth and Santhya: the tree's flowers, leaves and branches are the essence (ਤਤੁ) itself
decided because: the next line's names (all-pervading light, Nirankar, Sambhu) describe the Lord, the root, which fits the Darpan; the sense differs little

issue: ਸਿਖਵੰਤੇ
our reading: you who seek instruction (Darpan, Shabdarth, Faridkot)
alternatives: Santhya: one who holds and gives teaching, a would-be teacher with whom the Guru is in dialogue
decided because: three of four sources; ਸਿਖ here is the teaching received, the line tells him to listen

issue: ਤਿਸੁ ਕਾਰਣਿ ਕੰਮੁ ਨ ਧੰਧਾ
our reading: because of that (remembrance of God, Darpan), no work or business binds him
alternatives: Faridkot and Santhya: for that Guru no deed is a cause of worldly gain; Sant Singh Khalsa: he is not affected by actions and entanglements
decided because: the plain words: no work and no business for that reason; the Darpan's reading keeps the stanza's subject

issue: ਰਹਹਿ: who remains in Sunn Samadhi
our reading: you (God, 2nd sing.) remained in the trance of Sunn before creation (Darpan)
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh: some (3rd plural) remain absorbed in samadhi
decided because: line 6 describes the state before creation, when there was no water, land or sky; no one else existed to sit in samadhi

issue: ਨ ਜੋਤਿ ਅਪਾਰ
our reading: nor any other light (ਅਪਾਰ as ਅਪਰ, Darpan)
alternatives: nor the infinite light (of sun or moon) (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: the list is of what did not yet exist; boundless light would be God's own, who did; the Darpan's gloss avoids that

issue: ਐ ਜੀ: whom it addresses
our reading: by context, as the Darpan: the listener (lines 1, 5, 7, 11), the Guru (line 13), God (lines 15, 17); likewise 503.2 line 3 and 504.2
alternatives: one fixed rendering throughout
decided because: the address changes inside the shabad; one note in 503.2 explains the call

issue: ਕਰਹਿ ... ਕੇਤੇ
our reading: many (people) put on many garbs (3rd plural)
alternatives: Darpan: you (2nd sing.) put on many garbs
decided because: ਕੇਤੇ, many, names the subject; the line describes others, not the listener

issue: ਐ ਜੀਉ
our reading: O dear one, with the plural imperatives ਦਿੜਹੁ, ਲਾਵਹੁ
alternatives: Darpan: O my soul; Sant Singh Khalsa: implant the Naam within me
decided because: the plural imperatives address the listeners, as ਐ ਜੀ does elsewhere in the shabad

issue: ਜਲਾਈ
our reading: that Haumai may be burnt away by the Shabad
alternatives: Darpan: (the Guru) burns it; Sant Singh Khalsa: I have burnt my ego
decided because: the form allows both persons; the passive keeps the line's sense (the Shabad burns Haumai) without choosing

issue: ਹਿਰਦੈ ਕੰਠਿ ਬਣਾਈ
our reading: that he may make it the necklace of his heart (Darpan: ਕੰਠਿ, a necklace)
alternatives: adorn his heart and throat (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: the Darpan's gloss; ਬਣਾਈ, make, fits making a necklace

issue: ਰਵਿਆ
our reading: has remembered (Darpan, Faridkot)
alternatives: pervades (Sant Singh Khalsa; our word gloss)
decided because: with ਗੁਰਮਤਿ ਭ੍ਰਮਨਿ ਚੁਕਾਈ the line is about the seeker; two commentaries

issue: ਮਜਨੁ ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਭਾਈ
our reading: (the one to whom) the True Guru is pleasing takes the plunge (Darpan: ਭਾਈ, pleased)
alternatives: the True Guru is the bath attendant, O brother (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: ਭਾਈ ends every stanza of this shabad and 504.1 as a verb (pleases); there is no attendant in the line

issue: ਮਿਰਤ ਸੁਭ ਚਿੰਤੰ
our reading: death itself wishes well to one who dwells on the Lord through the Shabad
alternatives: Darpan: dying (to the vices) is for your good, so remember the Lord; Faridkot: reflect on the Shabad, being dead to the self
decided because: the plain words (death, well-wishing); two English translations read so

issue: ਤਉ ਸਰਣੀ
our reading: this body is in your (ਤਉ) refuge, said in prayer (Darpan, Faridkot)
alternatives: ਤਉ as then: then this body is in refuge
decided because: both commentaries; the line turns to God

issue: ਮਨੁ ਮਾਰਿ ... ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕਾ ਸਰਨੰ
our reading: Says Nanak: with the mind subdued, (I have come) to your refuge, O Pure One
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, subdue your mind and say, O Pure One, I am in your refuge; Sant Singh Khalsa: subdue my mind, O Lord
decided because: the settled rule renders ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ as says Nanak; ਮਾਰਿ read as the conjunct participle

issue: ਵਿਰਤਿ ਪਖਿ ਕਰਮੀ
our reading: gods and men dance on the side of worldly life, through their deeds (Faridkot: as doers of rites)
alternatives: Darpan: by (God's) grace (ਕਰਮਿ), even while at worldly work
decided because: the stanza lists all who dance, high and low; ਕਰਮੀ beside ਵਿਰਤਿ is the deeds of worldly life

issue: ਤਰੁ ਤਾਰੀ
our reading: swim across through the Lord's praise (Darpan: ਤਾਰੀ, a swim)
alternatives: the Lord's praise is a boat to carry you across (Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: ਤਰੁ is an imperative and ਤਾਰੀ its object, swimming

issue: ਭਗਤ ਜਨਾ ਕੀ ਊਤਮ ਬਾਣੀ
our reading: the word of the devotees is sublime (Darpan, Sant Singh Khalsa)
alternatives: they sing the sublime bani of the devotees
decided because: the sentence then turns to what they sing (the Indescribable's story); two sources

issue: ਜੋ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੀ ਅਤਿ ਪਿਆਰੀ (line 19): the Darpan supplies the praise (ਸਿਫ਼ਤਿ-ਸਾਲਾਹ) as what is dear to God; the Faridkot Teeka and Manmohan Singh the Saadh Sangat. Neither ਜਸੁ nor ਸਾਧਸੰਗੁ is feminine in form.
our reading: In the Saadh Sangat, which is most dear to God, Nanak has sung (his) praise. (the review's fix, kept)
alternatives: Nanak has sung in the Saadh Sangat the praise that is most dear to God (Darpan).
decided because: The feminine ਪਿਆਰੀ fits ਸੰਗਤਿ, the sense of ਸਾਧਸੰਗਿ, more naturally than masculine ਜਸੁ; the Faridkot Teeka reads so; the sense for the reader (singing in the holy company, dear to God) holds either way.

issue: ਕੋਮਨ ਸਿਰਿ ਕੋਮਾ: Sahib Singh reads ਕੋਮਾ as one of high lineage (you are the highest-born among the high-born); Santhya and Faridkot read ਕੌਮ / ਜਾਤ (your people is above all peoples).
our reading: over all the noble clans, yours is the noblest / ਸਭ ਉੱਚੀਆਂ ਕੁਲਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਿਰ ਉੱਤੇ ਤੇਰੀ ਕੁਲ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚੀ ਹੈ
alternatives: above the high-born you are the highest-born; your people (the saints) are above all peoples (Santhya's second reading)
decided because: A wording that holds both main readings (ਕੋਮ, ਕੌਮ, clan) without adding the Santhya's saints; the litany's pattern (X among Xs) is kept.

issue: ਨਾਮਨ ਮਹਿ ਤੇਰੋ ਪ੍ਰਭ ਨਾਮਾ: Sahib Singh reads ਨਾਮਾ as renown (ਨਾਮਣਾ: among the renowned yours is the renown); Faridkot and Manmohan Singh read names.
our reading: Among names, O God, yours is the Name
alternatives: Among the renowned, your renown is the greatest
decided because: The plain sense of ਨਾਮ and the Faridkot Teeka; nothing in the grammar requires the narrower sense of fame.

issue: ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਮਰਥ ... ਸਹਜ ਸਮਾਧਿ: Sahib Singh reads a prayer (by remembering you may I keep my attention in the samadhi of Sahaj); Manmohan Singh and SSK a command.
our reading: Remember the Almighty every moment and every instant; meditation on God is the samadhi of Sahaj.
alternatives: By remembering you every moment, may I keep my attention in the samadhi of Sahaj (Sahib Singh).
decided because: ਸਿਮਰਿ with ਸਮਰਥ as its object reads most plainly as an imperative; the second half is a nominal clause.

issue: ਰਖੁ ਧਰਮ: preserve my faith (Faridkot: the servant's dharma; SSK, Manmohan Singh) or keep my honour (Sahib Singh: ਲਾਜ ਰੱਖ).
our reading: keep my faith (safe from them) / (ਇਹਨਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਮੇਰਾ) ਧਰਮ ਬਚਾ ਰੱਖ
alternatives: keep my honour from them
decided because: ਧਰਮ is not ਪਤਿ; the word's own sense (faith, dharma) is kept.

issue: ਦੇਤ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਸ੍ਰਵਨ ਹਰਿ ਜਸੁ ਰਸਨ ਨਾਮ ਉਚਾਰ: Sahib Singh reads ਦੇਤ as governing all three (he gives his sight, his praise to the ears, the Name to the tongue); SSK, Manmohan Singh and Faridkot: he gives his sight to those who hear his praise and utter his Name.
our reading: (The Lord) grants the sight of himself, his praise to the ears, the utterance of the Name to the tongue;
alternatives: He grants his sight to those whose ears hear his praise and whose tongues utter his Name.
decided because: The three nouns stand side by side under the one verb ਦੇਤ with no relative word; the parallel reading needs nothing supplied.

issue: ਅੰਗ ਸੰਗ ਭਗਵਾਨ ਪਰਸਨ ਪ੍ਰਭ ... ਪਤਿਤ ਉਧਾਰ: whether ਪਰਸਨ (touch) is the devotees' touching of God or God's touch, which saves the fallen.
our reading: the Lord is ever beside (them), close to every limb; O Nanak, God's touch saves the fallen.
alternatives: They feel the Lord's presence and touch; God is the saviour of sinners (SSK, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: Sahib Singh's ਪਦਅਰਥ (ਪਰਸਨ: ਛੁਹ) and the line's order: ਪਰਸਨ ਪ੍ਰਭ ... ਪਤਿਤ ਉਧਾਰ.

issue: ਨਦਰੀ: the Gracious One (Sahib Singh's ਪਦਅਰਥ) or by (his) grace (SSK).
our reading: the Gracious One dwells in (their) minds
alternatives: by his grace the Lord dwells in the mind
decided because: Darpan's grammar takes ਨਦਰੀ as the noun, subject of ਵਸੈ; the sense is the same.

issue: ਤੁਰੀਆ ਸੁਖੁ ਪਾਇਆ: whose peace, and the tense: Sahib Singh supplies (one who reached) the turiya state found peace; Faridkot the same; SSK makes peace too a thing God made.
our reading: He made the root of Maya; (but) peace was found (only) in the fourth state (turiya).
alternatives: He created the root of Maya, and the peace of the fourth state (SSK).
decided because: ਪਾਇਆ is found, obtained, not created; the line sets Maya against the fourth state, beyond the three qualities of the line before.

issue: ਸਹਜੇ ਆਵਉ ਜਾਉ: first person (I come and go) or impersonal (one can come and go easily: Sahib Singh, SSK).
our reading: in Sahaj I come and go (through it) freely
alternatives: one passes through it easily
decided because: ਆਵਉ ਜਾਉ are first-person singular forms.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਸਤਿਗੁਰ ਸੋ ਧਨੁ ਸਉਪਿਆ: Sahib Singh reads ਸਤਿਗੁਰ (no sihari) as the dative (the Lord entrusted the wealth to the True Guru; it is in the Guru's soul); Faridkot, SSK and Manmohan Singh as the agent (the True Guru gave them the wealth that abides in their hearts).
our reading: O Nanak, (the Lord) has entrusted to the True Guru that wealth which abides within his very being; (whoever receives it from the Guru) is dyed in a deep colour (of love)
alternatives: The True Guru has bestowed on them the wealth that remains in their hearts; they are dyed deep in love.
decided because: The agent would be ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ; the bare form is the dative, as Sahib Singh's grammar shows. The sense for the reader is the same: the wealth comes through the Guru.

issue: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਬੋਲਾਤਾ: the Lord makes (one) speak his praise through the Guru (Sahib Singh: ਬੋਲਾਤਾ = ਬੁਲਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ), or the Gurmukh speaks of it (SSK, Faridkot).
our reading: Great is the glory of the Great One: through the Guru he makes (us) speak (his praise).
alternatives: The Gurmukh speaks of the great greatness of the Great Lord.
decided because: ਬੋਲਾਤਾ is the causative (makes speak), not ਬੋਲਤਾ; ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ as the settled adverb, through the Guru.

issue: ਪਉਣੈ ਪੁਛਹੁ ਜਾਇ: Faridkot has Dharam Raj tell his messengers to go and ask the soul; Sahib Singh and SSK: go and ask the soul (breath), whose answer is the next two lines.
our reading: The body is dust, and blind; go and ask the breath (the soul). (It answers:) I, lured by Maya, ...
alternatives: Dharam Raj's messengers are sent to ask the soul (Faridkot).
decided because: The line names no Dharam Raj; the plain words are kept, with the change of speaker named in line 4.

issue: ਚੀਰਾ: Darpan ਪੱਲਾ, ਆਸਰਾ; Faridkot ਪਾੜਾ (expanse) or ਪਟਾ (decree); the English refs 'projection, extension'.
our reading: everything rests on his support
alternatives: all is his expanse; all is under his decree
decided because: The Darpan's gloss (the hem one holds, support) fits the line's pairing with ਤਿਸ ਕੈ ਵਸਿ; the others are guesses from an obscure word.

issue: Structure of ਸਤੁ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ਸਭੁ ਸਚੁ ਹੈ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਪਵਿਤਾ: ਸਭੁ ਸਚੁ read as 'the True One everywhere' (Darpan: ਸਭੁ ਹਰ ਥਾਂ, ਸਚੁ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ) or as 'all truth'.
our reading: The Gurmukh is made pure: he gains sat and contentment, and sees the True One everywhere.
alternatives: The Gurmukh is all truthfulness and contentment, wholly true and pure (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: ਸਚੁ with aunkar is the noun, the True One, as everywhere in this vaar; ਸਭੁ as adverb follows the Darpan's grammar.

issue: ਭਗਤੀ: 'through devotion' (singular person, Darpan) or 'the devotees' (Faridkot, both English refs).
our reading: (one who) has earned it through devotion
alternatives: the devotees have earned it
decided because: Lines 2-6 speak of one person (ਆਪਿ ਤਰਿਆ, ਜਣੇਦੀ … ਉਸ ਦੀ), so the Darpan's reading keeps the stanza one sentence about one person.

issue: ਕੁਲ ਜਗਤੁ: 'the whole world' (ਕੁਲ, no aunkar, adjective: Darpan and both English refs) or 'his family and the world' (Faridkot).
our reading: has carried the whole world across
alternatives: carries his family and the world across
decided because: ਕੁਲ without aunkar is not the noun ਕੁਲੁ (family line, as in 28.1, 138.5); read as the adjective whole.

issue: ਛਾਦਨੁ ਭੋਜਨੁ ਨ ਲੈਹੀ ਸਤ ਭਿਖਿਆ: the Darpan reads 'alms given in faith' that they refuse (scorning what is given); others 'true alms'.
our reading: They will not accept clothing and food given as alms in good faith
alternatives: They do not accept the true alms (of the Name) / honest alms
decided because: ਸਤ ਭਿਖਿਆ as alms given in good faith keeps the plain sense; the refusal is the pride of the previous line.

issue: ਮਿਲਣਾ ਸੰਜੋਗੀ: the body is obtained by good fortune (Darpan, Faridkot) or union (with God) comes by destiny.
our reading: obtained only by good fortune
alternatives: meeting (God) in it comes by destiny
decided because: The line is about the body-fortress; all the commentaries read the obtaining of the body.

issue: ਨਿਰਜੋਗੁ ਹਰਿ ਜੋਗੀ: Darpan 'the Lord, the yogi, is unattached'; Faridkot and the English refs read a paradox, unattached yet joined (to all).
our reading: the Lord is free of all ties and yet joined (with all)
alternatives: the Lord, the yogi, is free of ties
decided because: The line answers the line before (he dwells in the body and enjoys its pleasures): the pairing ਨਿਰਜੋਗੁ / ਜੋਗੀ is a contrast, as Faridkot reads it.

issue: ਅਭਿਮਾਨੀ: 'of the proud' (Darpan, Faridkot: the proud one's body-fortress) or 'pride' as a third door (the English refs).
our reading: In the body-fortress of the proud are hard doors of falsehood and deceit
alternatives: doors of falsehood, deceit and pride
decided because: ਅਭਿਮਾਨੀ is the agent noun (the proud one), not the abstract noun ਅਭਿਮਾਨੁ.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਜਪਾਨੀ: those who repeat (Darpan), or 'and then one repeats the Name' (English refs), or 'by repeating' (Faridkot).
our reading: opened (for those) who repeat the Lord's Name
alternatives: the doors are opened, and then one repeats the Name
decided because: ਜਪਾਨੀ is a plural participle naming the people, as ਭੇਖਵਾਨੀ in the line before names the garb-wearers.

issue: ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ ਕਰਮੀ ਬੋਲੈ ਬੋਲਾਇ: by grace one speaks as (God) has one speak (Darpan), or the fortunate say it and make others say it (Faridkot, Manmohan Singh).
our reading: Only by (God's) grace does (one) say Waah Waah, as (he himself) has it said.
alternatives: The fortunate say Waah Waah and make others say it.
decided because: The saloks keep saying that God has the praise said (514.2.1, 514.3.3); ਬੋਲਾਇ is read with that subject.

issue: ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ ਸਤਿ ਰਜਾਇ: 'Waah Waah is the True One's will' (Sant Singh Khalsa), 'praise keeps one in his will' (Darpan), 'Waah Waah comes by the True One's will' (Faridkot).
our reading: Waah Waah comes only by the True One's will
alternatives: Waah Waah is the True One's will; praise keeps one within his will
decided because: Following line 4 (by grace one says it, as he has it said), the will is the source of the praise; the Faridkot reading fits the run of the salok.

issue: Line 2: ਗੁਰ ਕੈ ਸਬਦਿ ਵੀਚਾਰਿ ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਹਰਿ ਜਪੁ ਜਾਪਣਾ: the means by which she finds her Husband, or what she does once she has found him.
our reading: Kept: (it is) by reflecting on the Guru's Shabad and repeating the Lord's Name night and day.
alternatives: Darpan: the soul-bride who reflects through the Shabad and remembers the Lord daily becomes noble (as the Gujri did on finding her Husband); Faridkot: an exhortation, reflect on the Guru's Shabad and chant night and day.
decided because: ਵੀਚਾਰਿ is an absolutive and ਜਾਪਣਾ an infinitive; every reading makes the reflection and the repetition the way to the Husband, which ours states without adding a command the line does not have.

issue: Line 1: ਜਿਨਿ ਕੀਤੀ ਸੋ ਲੈ ਜਾਇ: what the Maker takes away.
our reading: Kept: hope and desire will die (only when) he who made them takes them away.
alternatives: Faridkot: when the Lord who made the creation takes away the soul, the hope in the mind goes of itself.
decided because: The Darpan reads ਕੀਤੀ as (ਆਸਾ ਮਨਸਾ) ਪੈਦਾ ਕੀਤੀ and ਲੈ ਜਾਇ as ਨਾਸ ਕਰੇ; the feminine ਕੀਤੀ agrees with ਆਸਾ ਮਨਸਾ, while the soul is not named in the line.

issue: Note on ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ: the term first appears in the Gujri vaar's earlier saloks (batch 06, 514.x), which may already carry the raag's note.
our reading: Note given here at 514.8.
alternatives: Drop this note if batch 06 already explains ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ; keep one note in the raag.
decided because: A missing note is harder to spot than a duplicate; reviewers keep the earlier one.

issue: ਸਬਾਹਿ
our reading: bringing, delivering (sustenance to all): ਪਹੁੰਚਾ ਕੇ
alternatives: Darpan: ਇਕੱਠਾ ਕਰ ਕੇ (gathering); a reading from Persian subah (every morning).
decided because: Faridkot and the Shabdarth both gloss ਪਹੁੰਚਾ ਕੇ / ਪੁਚਾ ਕੇ; it fits ਦੇਦਾ ਰਿਜਕੁ best.

issue: ਗੁਣਦਾਤਾ ਮਤਿ ਧੀਰੁ
our reading: the giver of virtues, steady in understanding (ਧੀਰੁ, masculine with aunkar, qualifies God)
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa: giver of virtue, intelligence and patience (ਮਤਿ and ਧੀਰ as gifts).
decided because: ਧੀਰੁ with aunkar is a masculine adjective of the subject, as the Darpan and the Shabdarth read it.

issue: ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ at the head of lines with ਹੈ (515.4, 515.6)
our reading: An exclamation of praise: Waah Waah! The Master is true …
alternatives: Darpan: the praise (ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ) is itself the True Lord's form; Sant Singh Khalsa: Waaho! Waaho! is the True Lord Master.
decided because: The exclamation reads every line of both saloks plainly and in one way (515.6 lines 2–3 can only be exclamations); where ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ is the object (515.6 lines 5–6) it is rendered as the praise received.

issue: ਵਾਹੁ ਵਾਹੁ ਬਾਣੀ ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ ਹੈ
our reading: Waah Waah! The Bani is the Word of the Formless One (ਨਿਰੰਕਾਰ genitive).
alternatives: Darpan: the bani of praise is the Formless One's own form; Faridkot: this Waah Waah bani is the Formless One's.
decided because: The genitive is the plain sense of the words and is read by Faridkot and Sant Singh Khalsa; it keeps the exclamation reading of the salok.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਤਿਨੑ ਕੈ ਸੰਗਿ ਮਿਲਾਇ
our reading: a prayer: O Lord, join (me) to their company, (that) I may utter Waah Waah (line 5's first person ਉਚਰਾ, ਕਰੇਉ)
alternatives: Sahib Singh (refs): those servants meet the Lord; Sant Singh Khalsa as ours.
decided because: The Darpan's full text and Faridkot read the prayer, and line 5's first-person verbs need it.

issue: ਦੂਜੀ ਨਾਹੀ ਜਾਇ
our reading: there is no other place (to find peace): ਜਾਇ = place
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa: the sense of duality does not depart.
decided because: ਦੂਜੀ is feminine, agreeing with ਜਾਇ (place, feminine); Darpan and Faridkot read it so.

issue: ਗੂਜਰੀ ਜਾਤਿ ਗਵਾਰਿ
our reading: a Gujri, a woman of rustic caste (the Gujjar milkmaid), when she finds her own Husband …
alternatives: Faridkot's first reading: O fool, (your life) is passing (ਗੁਜ਼ਰਨਾ); Faridkot's second: the Gujri gopis who won Krishna.
decided because: ਜਾਤਿ and ਗਵਾਰਿ carry sihari, so neither 'is passing' nor a vocative fits (Darpan, Santhya); no allusion to Krishna is in the words, so none is written into the meaning.

issue: ਜਿਨਿ ਏਹੁ ਲੇਖਾ ਲਿਖਿਆ
our reading: whoever has written this account (in the mind), i.e. taken it in
alternatives: Darpan: understood this; Faridkot: reflected on true and false.
decided because: Kept the verse's image of writing, with the implied 'in the mind' in brackets; all readings agree on the sense.

issue: Who speaks in pauri 20 (ਪਾਇਆ, ਧਿਆਇਆ, ਮਿਟਾਇਆ have no subject)
our reading: First person (my prayer, I have received …), and line 5: Nanak has become free of care.
alternatives: Darpan: general (if one prays …, one becomes carefree).
decided because: Faridkot and both published translations read the devotee's own account; ਭਏ in line 5 goes with Nanak (honorific plural).

issue: ਘਰੁ ਉਚਾ ਨਿਰਣਉ
our reading: (the embankments are high) with an eye on the high house, the cloud (ਨਿਰਣਉ: having made out, watched)
alternatives: Faridkot and Santhya: in the field with high embankments the cloud's water stays, (this is) settled (ਨਿਰਣੈ); Shabdarth: I gaze at the high house.
decided because: ਨਿਰਣਉ (Sanskrit nirṇaya, ascertaining) as 'having made out' gives the farmer's familiar practice the Darpan describes and joins line 2's simile; the image is explained in a note.

issue: ਸਜਣ ਪਾਹੁਣਿਅਉ
our reading: the Friend (the Lord, honorific) comes as a guest
alternatives: Santhya: ਸਜਣ is plural here, the saints come as guests; Faridkot: saints or good qualities.
decided because: The Darpan and the Shabdarth read the Beloved; the salok ends with finding the Lord within the mind.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਜਾਣੀਐ
our reading: through the Guru this (what is truly sweet and who is a friend) is known by the one whom God himself enlightens (ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ adverb)
alternatives: Santhya, Faridkot, Sant Singh Khalsa: he is known as a Gurmukh whom the Lord enlightens.
decided because: Settled rendering of ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ as 'through the Guru'; the Darpan reads it so and it completes line 1.

issue: ਸਭਿ ਕਿਲਵਿਖ ਕਾਟੁ
our reading: a command: cut away all sins
alternatives: Shabdarth: (meditate on the Naam of him who is) the cutter of all sins.
decided because: ਕਾਟੁ parallels the imperative ਧਿਆਇ in the same sentence; the Darpan reads the command.

issue: Heading ਰਾਗੁ ਗੂਜਰੀ ਵਾਰ ਮਹਲਾ ੫
our reading: Raag Gujri Vaar: by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). / ਰਾਗ ਗੂਜਰੀ ਵਾਰ: ਪੰਜਵੇਂ ਗੁਰੂ … ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ।
alternatives: Raag Gujri, Vaar, by the Fifth Guru …
decided because: Follows the vaar-heading pattern (title, colon, by the … Guru) with the title as the line names it; reconcile with the batch that renders Gujri ki Vaar M3's heading (508).

issue: ਤਿਸੁ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਕੀ ਟੇਕ ਨਾਨਕ ਮਨੈ ਮਾਹਿ
our reading: a statement: in Nanak's mind is the support of that Master
alternatives: Santhya and Sant Singh Khalsa: a command, O Nanak, hold (his support) in your mind.
decided because: No imperative verb is in the line; the Darpan reads the statement.

issue: Subject of ਪਾਹਿ, ਕਮਾਹਿ, ਸਮਾਹਿ (third plural, unnamed)
our reading: (we)
alternatives: Darpan: beings (ਜੀਵ); Sant Singh Khalsa: I / Nanak.
decided because: An unnamed plural subject; (we) reads naturally in a prayer addressed to God and keeps line 4's O Nanak.

issue: ਮਨ ਕਉ ਹੋਇ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ਧਿਆਈਐ ਸਦਾ ਹਰਿ: ਧਿਆਈਐ as an injunction (should be meditated on) or as the condition (when / if one meditates).
our reading: condition: the mind finds contentment when the Lord is meditated on always
alternatives: a separate injunction: the mind finds contentment; the Lord should be meditated on always (the draft and the review)
decided because: ਧਿਆਈਐ carries both senses; here the clause stands beside ਹੋਇ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ in one line as its cause, as in the parallel 519.3 line 6 (ਮਨ ਕਉ ਹੋਇ ਸੰਤੋਖੁ ਭੁਖਾ ਧ੍ਰਾਪੀਐ), and the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka and the other translations all read it as the condition.

issue: Whose love (ਹਿਤੁ) is not hidden, and from whom.
our reading: However many my wrong ways, your love (for me) does not stay hidden; line 2: you, the Husband, have covered them.
alternatives: Darpan: our many wrong deeds and our love of them are not hidden from you (God sees them), yet you cover them. Faridkot: our many wrong acts are not hidden from you.
decided because: ਹਿਤੁ is the singular subject of ਗੁਝਾ ਥੀਐ ਨ, and ਕਿਤੀਆ ਕੁਢੰਗ reads as a concessive (however many); the Santhya reads so, and line 2 (you have covered them) completes it: in spite of the faults, the Lord's love shows in his covering them.

issue: ਮਰਉ ਵਿਚਾਰੀ ਸੂਲਿ: who dies, and what.
our reading: I, poor one, am dying in pain (the speaker, set against those who please God).
alternatives: Santhya, Faridkot: the pain (ਸੂਲਿ) of those who please God dies away, helpless.
decided because: ਮਰਉ is first person singular (as ਮਾਗਉ, ਕਰਉ, ਪੇਖਉ in this vaar), ਵਿਚਾਰੀ is feminine agreeing with the soul-bride speaking, and ਸੂਲਿ with sihari is locative (in pain); the Darpan's reading.

issue: ਸੰਤ ਪਿਆਰੇ: one Sant (the Guru) or the Sants.
our reading: the beloved Sants
alternatives: Darpan: the beloved Guru (singular).
decided because: The form is open to either; the Faridkot reads the Sants, and the plural keeps to the words without supplying the Guru.

issue: ਆਹਿ: is, or long for.
our reading: is: (such) is that Husband Lord on whose support everyone rests.
alternatives: Santhya (and our word list): ਆਹਿ = long for; O Nanak, long for that Lord on whose support all are.
decided because: The Darpan and the Faridkot read ਆਹਿ as the verb is (Lahndi aahe), and line 1 sets out the image this line names: the Lord who keeps earth in water and fire in wood is the one on whom all rest.

issue: ਖੋਜੀ: through the tracker (the Guru), or as a seeker myself; whose tracks.
our reading: Through the tracker (the Guru) I have found the tracks of those who had laid my field waste.
alternatives: Santhya: by searching (within myself) I found the tracks; Faridkot: as a seeker I found the trace of the Self and left the wilderness.
decided because: ਖੋਜੀ with the field, the fence and the ruin of line 2 is the village tracker who follows the footprints of the ones who trampled a field; the Darpan's reading, and it keeps the image whole.

issue: ਚਿਤਾਰਿ ਮਨ: O mind, or in the mind.
our reading: remembering (him) in the mind, I find peace
alternatives: Darpan: O mind, praise the Perfect Guru, (through whom) remembering (the Naam) brings peace.
decided because: ਲਹਾ is first person (I find); remembering in the mind is the plainer construction and the Faridkot's.

issue: ਹੁੰਮਸ ਧੁੰਮਸ
our reading: stifling heat and turmoil
alternatives: Darpan: the great heat of the fire (of craving); Santhya: suffocation and darkness; Faridkot: beating and uproar.
decided because: In Punjabi ਹੁੰਮਸ is stifling heat and ਧੁੰਮਸ commotion, a jingle for oppressive turmoil; the Punjabi keeps the words themselves.

issue: ਘਟੇ ਘਟਿ ਸਾਰਿਆ: fills every heart, or takes care of every heart.
our reading: He fills every single heart (ਹਰੇਕ ਘਟ ਵਿੱਚ ਭਰਪੂਰ ਹੈ), as written.
alternatives: Darpan ਪਦਅਰਥ: ਸਾਰਿਆ, ਸੰਭਾਲ ਕਰਦਾ ਹੈ (pervading each heart, he takes care of each).
decided because: The line pairs it with ਊਣਾ ਕਹੀ ਨ ਹੋਇ (nowhere lacking): presence is the sense; the Faridkot Teeka (ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਹੈਂ) and the Shabad OS Sahib Singh line (ਮੌਜੂਦ ਹੈ) read it so; the Darpan too has him pervading every heart first.

issue: ਦੁਹਾ ਸਿਰਿਆ: which two ends.
our reading: Both ends, this world and the next.
alternatives: Darpan: both sides, the pull of Maya and the savour of the Name; Santhya: birth and death, this world and the next.
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka and the Santhya read lok and parlok; it is the plainer sense of both ends, and the Darpan's pairing is drawn from the earlier saloks, not from this line.

issue: ਕਰਮ ਧਰਮ ਤਤੁ ਗਿਆਨੁ: a list of three, or the knowledge that is the essence of rites and duties.
our reading: Deeds, dharam and the knowledge of the essence all come with the company of the Sants.
alternatives: Darpan: the lofty understanding which is the essence of all rites and duties comes in the company of the Sants (as at 260.2, ਕਰਮ ਧਰਮ ਤਤੁ ਨਾਮ ਅਰਾਧੂ).
decided because: Here ਤਤੁ stands beside ਗਿਆਨੁ, both nominative, as one term (tatva-gyan, knowledge of the essence), where at 260.2 ਤਤੁ is the predicate; the Santhya and the Faridkot Teeka read the three as a list, and the pauri sets the company of the Sants above all other means.

issue: ਗਰੀਬ ਨਿਵਾਜਿ: a participle (having honoured the lowly) or the instrumental of the name Garib-nivaj (by the Cherisher of the lowly).
our reading: Honouring the lowly and setting them firm, he has given his own protection.
alternatives: Santhya, Faridkot: the Cherisher of the poor has established (us) and given his protection.
decided because: The Darpan reads ਨਿਵਾਜਿ, ਥਾਪਿ and ਕਾਪਿ (next line) as parallel conjunct participles; the sense is the same either way.

issue: Who are the brave warriors whom no one has held back.
our reading: The five vices themselves are the warriors; no one has checked them.
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh: even brave and mighty men cannot withstand the army of the five.
decided because: ਕਿਨੈ ਨ ਹੋੜੀਐ (no one has stopped) has the warriors as its object; the Darpan and the Santhya both take them as the vices.

issue: ਗੁਣ ਗਾਉ: a command or a verbal noun.
our reading: A command: sing his praises day after day, (and) all sins are washed away.
alternatives: By singing his praises daily all sins are washed away (one Sahib Singh text, the Faridkot Teeka, the English translations).
decided because: ਗਾਉ is the imperative form; the Darpan's arth reads it as a command; the sense is the same.

issue: ਜੀਉ: imperative live, vocative O soul, or a noun (spiritual life is gained).
our reading: Imperative: making the effort, live (the true life); practising, enjoy peace; meditating, meet God.
alternatives: Darpan: in making the effort spiritual life is gained; Santhya: O soul, in effort and practice enjoy peace.
decided because: ਜੀਉ ਤੂੰ stands parallel to ਸੁਖ ਭੁੰਚੁ and ਤੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਭੂ ਮਿਲੁ, both imperatives, each after a participle in -ਦਿਆ; the Faridkot Teeka reads it so.

issue: ਸਚਿ ਸਮਾਹਰਾ: who is absorbed, and in what.
our reading: The Lord dwells in the devotees' minds and through Truth is absorbed in them.
alternatives: Faridkot: you, the True, blissful (ਸਮਾਹਰਾ as joyful) Lord, dwell in the devotees' minds; others: the devotees are absorbed in the True One.
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਸਮਾਹਰਾ as ਸਮਾਇਆ ਹੋਇਆ, agreeing with ਸੋ (he); the subject of both verbs is the Lord.

issue: Is the pauri addressed to God (you are the Protector) or about him.
our reading: Spoken of God in the third person, with Nanak as subject in the last line.
alternatives: Faridkot, Santhya, Sant Singh Khalsa: the -ਆ endings (ਵਾਲਿਆ, ਅਪਾਰਿਆ) as vocatives, the pauri addressed to God.
decided because: The verbs (ਹੋਇ, ਘਾਲਿਆ, ਪਾਲਿਆ, ਵੁਠਾ ਆਪਿ) are third person throughout, as the Darpan reads them; the -ਆ endings are the rhyme of the pauri.

issue: ਆਪੇ ਹੀ ਘਾਲਿਆ.
our reading: He himself makes (us) do the labour of devotion.
alternatives: Faridkot: you yourself have destroyed (the manmukhs); Santhya notes also: he himself has done (it).
decided because: The Darpan and the Santhya's main reading agree; the Faridkot reading needs an object the line does not have.

issue: Whom the Supreme God has protected.
our reading: His servant, the subject of the third-person verbs that follow (ਰਵੈ, ਭਵੈ).
alternatives: Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh: me (first person throughout).
decided because: Lines 3 and 4 have third-person singular verbs; the Darpan supplies the servant.

issue: Whose wishes are fulfilled and who found the treasure: Nanak himself or the devotee in general.
our reading: First person (my), Nanak's own testimony, closing with Nanak merged in the True One.
alternatives: Darpan: a general statement (the one who remembers), with O Nanak in the last line.
decided because: The past tenses (ਪਾਇਆ, ਭਾਲਦਾ, ਰਹਿਆ ਘਾਲਦਾ) tell of one seeker, and the last line ਨਾਨਕ ਸਚਿ ਸਮਾਇਆ has Nanak as subject (style §12); the Faridkot Teeka reads the pauri in the first person.

issue: ਰਹਿਆ ਘਾਲਦਾ.
our reading: The toil is over (the striving has ceased).
alternatives: Kept striving (the earlier labour that led to the merging).
decided because: ਰਹਿਆ here is ceased, as the Darpan (ਮਿਹਨਤ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਨਾਹ ਰਹੀ) and the Faridkot Teeka read it.

issue: ਨਾਉ ਨਾਨਕ ਬਖਸੀਸ: Nanak's prayer for the gift, or those who know the Hukam string the Name into their minds.
our reading: O Nanak, they string the Name, God's gift, into their minds.
alternatives: Faridkot: Nanak asks, grant me the gift of your Name and I will string it in my mind.
decided because: The line continues the subject of line 7 (those who recognise the Hukam) with the same infinitive in -ਣਾ; the Darpan reads it so.

review: Bithal vs Beethal (writer's open point). Settled: Bithal / ਬੀਠਲ. The house spelling writes ਈ as i in names (Kabir, Kirtan, Pitambar, Gujri, Beni), and Bithal is the majority in the live meanings (5 times in Asa 485.2 against Beethal twice, 92.1 and 205.1). Keep the batch as written; 92.1 (line 6 and its note) and 205.1 (line 2) are to change to Bithal.

Tilochan vs Trilochan (writer's open point). Settled as written: Tilochan / ਤਿਲੋਚਨ in line 11, as the line names him; Trilochan in the headings 525.4 (as it spells him) and 526.1 (bare ਗੂਜਰੀ ॥, named as the Bhagat's section heading and Sri Raag 92.1 name him) and in the note. No change.

Bhagat headings with a Ghar (writer's open point). Settled as written: the Ghar after the raag, then the form and the Bhagat as Asa and Gauri render them (Raag Gujri, Ghar 1, Pade of Sri Namdev Ji. / ਰਾਗ ਗੂਜਰੀ, ਘਰ ੧ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਨਾਮਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਪਦੇ।; bare ਗੂਜਰੀ ਘਰੁ ੩ ॥ Raag Gujri, Ghar 3, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.), matching the Gurus' Raag Gujri, Ghar N, … headings in batches 01-05. No change.

issue: ਜਿਨਿ ਤੀਨੈ ਜਰਿਆ: burned away the three fevers, or bore the three powers.
our reading: Who has burned away the three (fevers), as written.
alternatives: Faridkot: ਜਰਿਆ = ਸਹਾਰਿਆ, he who bears the three powers (creation, sustenance, dissolution).
decided because: The Darpan glosses ਜਰਿਆ ਸਾੜ ਦਿੱਤੇ ਹਨ and ਤੀਨੈ ਤਿੰਨੇ ਤਾਪ; ਜਰਨਾ in the sense of burning fits the praise of what the Lord does for his devotee, and the three fevers are already explained in this raag (502.1).

issue: ਤੇਲਕ ਕੇ ਕਪਿ: what the kapi is.
our reading: Like an oil-presser's ox going round and round.
alternatives: Darpan: like the oil-presser's (ox) and the monkey (caught by its fistful of grain, made to dance door to door); Faridkot's second reading: the monkey that takes red berries for fire and spends the night warming at them.
decided because: The line has one comparison (ਤੇਲਕ ਕੇ … ਜਿਉ, 'the oil-presser's … like'), and the oil-presser's animal is the ox; Santhya, Faridkot's first reading and the Shabdarth read it so, and the ox continues the shabad's own image (the Rahao's ox). Kept with a short note.

issue: Who speaks from line 5, and whether to name him.
our reading: The mother speaks lines 1-4 (she names Kabir in the third person); Kabir answers from line 5 ('I'), so the piece opens 'Kabir answers:' (style.md §3, speaker change not named in the verse).
alternatives: Darpan: the whole shabad is Kabir's own telling, no line is the mother's.
decided because: Lines 3-4 speak of Kabir in the third person and line 5 in the first; without naming the change the reader would take 'I' for the mother. Santhya marks the answer from line 5.

issue: ਪਦੁ ਨਿਰਬਾਨੁ: its relation to ਹਰਿ.
our reading: Worship the Lord, (in whom is) the state of nirvana.
alternatives: Santhya, SSK, MMS: worship the Lord and you will attain the state of nirvana; Faridkot: worship the Lord, the state of nirvana.
decided because: ਪਦੁ ਨਿਰਬਾਨੁ is a nominative beside ਹਰਿ with no verb of attaining; Darpan reads the Lord as (the giver of) that state. The result, no more coming and going, is in the next line.

issue: ਬੈਠੋ ਰੀ ਆਈ: where he has come and settled.
our reading: In every heart, like the fragrance in flowers.
alternatives: SSK, MMS: in my mind.
decided because: Darpan and Santhya: within all beings; the shabad is about the all-pervading Lord whom no one saw coming, not about the poet's own realisation.

issue: ਆਕੁਲੁ.
our reading: Fills all (all-pervading).
alternatives: Shabdarth, MMS, SSK: without lineage (a-kul).
decided because: Darpan (whose kul is every direction), Faridkot (ਪੂਰਨ) and Santhya (Marathi aakul, full) agree; it fits ਰਮਈਆ, the all-pervading.

issue: ਜਿਉ ਆਕਾਸੈ ਘੜੂਅਲੋ ਮ੍ਰਿਗ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨਾ ਭਰਿਆ.
our reading: A pot in the sky filled with mirage-water (cannot be grasped), the third of three things that cannot be seen or held.
alternatives: Darpan: as mirage-water seen in an open plain (ਆਕਾਸੈ = in the open), whose place is never reached.
decided because: The words say a ਘੜੂਅਲੋ (pot) in the ਆਕਾਸ; Faridkot, Santhya, Shabdarth and MMS keep the pot; the sense (not to be grasped) is the same.

issue: ਜਿਨਿ ਤੀਨੈ ਜਰਿਆ.
our reading: Who has burned away the three (fevers).
alternatives: Shabdarth, MMS, SSK: on whom the three comparisons fit; Faridkot: who bears the three powers (creation, sustenance, dissolution), or in whom the three examples are set; Santhya: a cloth woven of the three (ਜਰੀ).
decided because: ਜਿਨਿ is the agent (ergative) of the transitive ਜਰਿਆ: he did something to the three. Darpan reads ਜਰਿਆ as burnt and the three as the three taaps; 'fits the comparisons' leaves ਜਿਨਿ without its agent sense. Note added.

issue: Name of the Lord: ਬੀਠਲੋ.
our reading: Bithal / ਬੀਠਲ, as Raag Asa (485.2) spells Namdev's ਬੀਠਲੁ.
alternatives: Sri Raag 92.1 (Trilochan) renders ਬੀਠੁਲਾ as Beethal.
decided because: One name, one spelling: the two earlier raags differ; reviewers to settle across the Granth.

issue: Rahao ਅਵਰੁ ਨ ਫੂਲੁ ਅਨੂਪੁ ਨ ਪਾਵਉ.
our reading: I find no other flower, none beyond compare.
alternatives: Darpan: no other (pure) flower is to be had; shall I (then) not attain the Beautiful One (ਅਨੂਪੁ = the Lord)?
decided because: The two negatives sit in one line about the offering; the next stanzas go on about tainted offerings and the answer (body and mind) comes only in stanza 4. Faridkot, SSK and MMS take ਅਨੂਪੁ with the flower.

issue: ਕਵਨ ਗਤਿ ਮੋਰੀ: tense.
our reading: What, then, will my state be?
alternatives: Darpan: what would my state have been (if worship needed pure offerings)?
decided because: The line has no verb; a plain question about the speaker's lot follows from line 12 (worship with offerings is not mine to give). The sense of Darpan's reading is kept by 'then'.

issue: ਭਰਮੇ ਭੂਲੀ: the feminine subject.
our reading: (The world) has strayed in doubt.
alternatives: Faridkot: the intellect (ਬੁਧੀ) of the hypocrite in garb; MMS: the world.
decided because: Darpan's ਲੋਕਾਈ; the following line (has not recognised the Lord of bliss) fits the world led by garb.

issue: ਇਸਤ੍ਰੀ.
our reading: (His) wife.
alternatives: SSK, MMS: women / a woman.
decided because: The list is of one's own attachments: wealth, wife, sons, house (Darpan: ਆਪਣੀ ਇਸਤ੍ਰੀ).

issue: The Bhagat's name: ਤਿਲੋਚਨੁ (not ਤ੍ਰਿਲੋਚਨੁ) in the line.
our reading: Tilochan / ਤਿਲੋਚਨ, as the line names him (settled: a Bhagat named as the line names him); the heading of 526.1 and 525.4 keep Trilochan.
alternatives: Trilochan everywhere.
decided because: The settled rule; reviewers may prefer one name for the Bhagat.

issue: ਜਦਿਚਿੰਤਿ ਸਰਬ ਗਤੰ.
our reading: Beyond the reach of thought (yad + achintya), reaching everywhere.
alternatives: Shabdarth, SSK, MMS, Santhya's second: by contemplating whom all attain salvation; Faridkot's second: if you would contemplate, contemplate the one who reaches all.
decided because: Darpan and Santhya's first reading split ਜਦ+ਅਚਿੰਤਿ, and the line is a string of attributes (wondrous, beyond Prakriti …) ending in sarb-gatam, the all-reaching.

issue: ਜਸੁ ਸ੍ਵਸਤਿ ਸੁਕ੍ਰਿਤ ਕ੍ਰਿਤੰ.
our reading: Praise (the Lord): that is well-being, that is the good deed to do.
alternatives: Darpan: if you want glory (ਜਸੁ) and well-being, do good deeds; Santhya's second: if you desire glory, well-being, good deeds and success; Faridkot, SSK, MMS: do the good deed of praising the auspicious Lord.
decided because: The shabad's Rahao is the Name and its praise; ਜਸੁ in Gurbani is praise, and Faridkot and Santhya's first take it so. Recorded for review.

issue: ਜਦਿਬਿਧਿ ਆਚਰਣੰ.
our reading: Conduct that goes against what is right (yad + avidhi), to be given up.
alternatives: Santhya: conduct by ritual rule (vidhi-nishedh), also to be given up; MMS/SSK: the path of good conduct (sought).
decided because: Darpan and Faridkot split ਜਦ+ਅਬਿਧਿ; it stands in a list of evils (greed, eyeing another's home) that line 10 says to give up.

issue: ਹਰਿ ਭਗਤ ਨਿਜ ਨਿਹਕੇਵਲਾ: statement or command.
our reading: The Lord's own devotees are wholly pure in heart, deed and word.
alternatives: SSK, MMS: worship the immaculate Lord in thought, word and deed (a command).
decided because: There is no imperative in the line; ਭਗਤ ਨਿਜ is 'his own devotees' (Darpan), and line 12 asks what they gain by yoga, sacrifice, charity, austerity.

issue: ਜੈਦੇਵ ਆਇਉ ਤਸ ਸਫੁਟੰ ਭਵ ਭੂਤ ਸਰਬ ਗਤੰ.
our reading: Jaidev has come openly to his (refuge), who in present and past reaches all.
alternatives: MMS, SSK: who gives salvation to all, past, present and future.
decided because: ਸਰਬ ਗਤੰ repeats line 3's all-reaching (Darpan, Faridkot).

issue: ਹਰਿ ਭਾਵੈ ਤਿਤੁ ਰਾਹਿ ਚਲੀ: ਚਲੀ is feminine; the Darpan reads a third subject (the soul-bride who pleases the Lord walks that road), while the subject of the line's first half is Nanak.
our reading: On whatever road pleases the Lord, on that road he walks.
alternatives: The soul-bride who pleases the Lord walks that road (Darpan); I walk the road that pleases the Lord.
decided because: The line continues Nanak's own helplessness (ਕਿਆ ਕਰੈ ਬਿਚਾਰਾ); ਚਲੀ is the feminine of the speaker as bride, as in the Rahao (ਹਮ ਪੀਛੈ ਲਾਗਿ ਚਲੀ); the Faridkot and the other refs read Nanak walking; kept as written.

issue: Line 3 read alone (the Beloved's words are sweet to the heart) or as the relative clause the next line's ਓਹ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ needs.
our reading: She to whose heart the Beloved's words are sweet: this way of hers has become good.
alternatives: A first-person statement: the Beloved's words are sweet to my heart, this way is good.
decided because: ਓਹ ਸੁੰਦਰਿ in the next line points back to a woman already described; the Darpan and the Santhya read it so.

issue: ਲਟੁਰੀ ਮਧੁਰੀ: wayward and slight (Darpan: ਲਟੋਰ, ਆਪ-ਹੁਦਰੀ; ਛੋਟੀ, ਥੋੜ੍ਹ-ਵਿਤੀ), or charming and sweet-voiced (the Faridkot's second sense).
our reading: Wayward and slight as she may be, she has pleased the Master.
alternatives: Faridkot: either fickle and of little worth, or graceful and sweet of speech; the Santhya: whether bent at the waist or small.
decided because: The line stresses that the Master's pleasure, not her merit, decides (the shabad goes on: she who pleases the Husband is the good one); the Darpan's and the Faridkot's first sense agree.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ: vocative (Darpan: O servant Nanak, the Lord is found by the Guru's grace) or the subject of ਪਾਇਆ.
our reading: By the Guru's grace servant Nanak has found him: searching within the body, he has come upon the Lord.
alternatives: O servant Nanak, by the Guru's grace the Lord is found, found by searching within.
decided because: Nanak speaks of himself, the past tense ਪਾਇਆ / ਲਾਧਾ tells what happened (style.md §12: Nanak as subject).

issue: ਰਾਖਹੁ: a statement (you protect) or a request (protect him).
our reading: whoever comes into your refuge, you protect in your mercy.
alternatives: Whoever comes to your refuge, protect him, showing mercy.
decided because: ਜੋ … ਤਿਸੁ states a general truth about the refuge, which the next line then asks for Nanak (ਰਾਖਹੁ ਲਾਜ); the Darpan reads a statement.

issue: ਬਿਖੈ ਸੋਗ: sorrows from vice (ਬਿਖੈ = ਵਿਸ਼ੇ) or simply sorrows set beside joys (ਬਿਖੈ = in).
our reading: Here joys bloom, there are sorrows born of vice.
alternatives: Somewhere one flowers in joy, somewhere (one is) in grief.
decided because: The Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ glosses ਬਿਖੈ as ਵਿਸ਼ੇ-ਵਿਕਾਰ; a postposition after ਆਨੰਦ would leave ਫੂਲਹਿ without its plural subject.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ: vocative (Darpan) or the speaker naming himself.
our reading: Without virtue, unlovely and of no family am I, Nanak; (yet my) Husband, the Master, is bliss itself.
alternatives: O Nanak, I am without virtue …
decided because: The line is the speaker's own confession (ਹਉ), so Nanak speaks of himself (style.md §12).

issue: ਇਹ ਦੇਹੀ ਧਾਰੀ: the soul taking on bodies in birth after birth, or God fashioning bodies (Darpan).
our reading: Wherever this body was taken on, it never found a lasting stay.
alternatives: Wherever God has fashioned a body, no one has ever been able to stay for ever.
decided because: ਇਹ ਦੇਹੀ is this (one's own) body, and the line follows the soul's return to its source; read so it needs no added subject.

issue: ਤਾ ਸਿਉ ਪ੍ਰੀਤਿ ਘਟਾਵਉ: I lessen my love for them (Maya's shows), or because of them I lessen my love for God (Darpan).
our reading: Maya's many shows are in vain; I lessen my love for them.
alternatives: These many shows of Maya are vain, for which I am lessening my love for God.
decided because: ਤਾ ਸਿਉ is with them, the shows just named, and the shabad is the seeker's resolve to please God; the Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ itself glosses ਤਾ ਸਿਉ as ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨਾਲ.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਓਟ ਗਹੀ: Nanak has taken shelter (subject); the Darpan reads O Nanak, (the one who) takes shelter; the Santhya, the shelter of (Guru) Nanak.
our reading: Nanak has taken the shelter of the Master, who does and causes all to be done.
alternatives: O Nanak, (his cleverness ends) who takes the Master's shelter; or, the shelter of Guru Nanak was grasped.
decided because: ਗਹੀ needs a subject and the line names only Nanak, the signature of the speaker, who gives up his own cleverness; the shabad's Rahao is his own confession.

issue: Who is blind, dumb and lame: the speaker or all beings (Darpan).
our reading: (I am) blind, dumb, lame and without understanding; O God, the Protector, protect (me).
alternatives: (Beings) are blind, dumb, lame and witless; O God, protect them.
decided because: The next line ends ਕਿਆ ਨਾਨਕ ਜੰਤ ਬਿਚਾਰਾ: the helpless creature is Nanak himself.

issue: ਜਿਸੁ ਲੜਿ ਲਾਵੈ: whom God attaches to his own hem, or to the hem of the Sants (Darpan).
our reading: the one, O Nanak, whom (God) attaches to the hem of (his) robe.
alternatives: whom (God) attaches to the hem of his servants.
decided because: The line has no possessor; the usual sense of ਲੜਿ ਲਾਉਣਾ in Gurbani is God taking one into his own keeping, and the servants' company is already named in the line.

review: ਤੇਰੀ ਬਾਣੀ is the object of ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ beside ਨਾਮੁ (no postposition needed), as the Darpan, the Faridkot Teeka's second reading and Santhya all take it; ਬਲਿਹਾਰੇ with nothing after it is Nanak's sacrifice to the Lord addressed (ਤੇਰੀ). Nothing in the grammar bears out a sacrifice to the Bani.
reviewer_fix: Repeating the Naam, your Bani, again and again, I live; servant Nanak is a sacrifice (to you).

issue: ਤੇਰੀ ਬਾਣੀ goes with ਜਪਿ ਜਪਿ … ਜੀਵਾ (the Darpan: by uttering your Bani I live) or with ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਸ ਬਲਿਹਾਰੇ.
our reading: Repeating the Naam I live; servant Nanak is a sacrifice to your Bani.
alternatives: Darpan: living by repeating the Name and uttering your Bani; Santhya: your Name, which is your Bani.
decided because: The line divides at ਜੀਵਾ, and ਤੇਰੀ ਬਾਣੀ stands next to ਬਲਿਹਾਰੇ, with no postposition linking it to ਜਪਿ.

issue: ਤਾ ਕੀ ਬਿਖੈ ਅਧਾਰਾ: ਤਾਕੀ (looked to) and ਬਿਖੈ (poison of vice) in the Darpan and as the Santhya reads first; ਤਾ ਕੀ (his) and ਬਿਖੈ (in), as the Faridkot Teeka reads.
our reading: the devotees and servants have had their support in him.
alternatives: Darpan: they have looked to you for support to escape vice; Santhya: amid Maya you have been their support.
decided because: Our text separates ਤਾ ਕੀ, and ਬਿਖੈ as the postposition (in) needs no added words; the Faridkot Teeka and Santhya option (a) read it so.

issue: ਬਾਲ ਗੁਪਾਲ: the Lord's children (the Darpan, the Shabdarth) or a Gopal-like child (Santhya, which ties the shabad to a child's recovery).
our reading: the children of Gopal are saved.
alternatives: the child, (dear as) Gopal, has been saved.
decided because: ਉਬਰੇ is plural, and the shabad names no event; the plain reading needs no history.

issue: ਵਰ ਨਾਰੀ ਮਿਲਿ: the bride meeting the Husband (the Darpan, the Shabdarth) or the excellent women, the devotees, gathering (Santhya).
our reading: United with the Husband (the Lord), the bride has sung songs of rejoicing.
alternatives: The noble women (the devotees) gathered and sang songs of joy.
decided because: ਵਰ is the bridegroom in Gurbani's usage, and two of the three readings take it so.

issue: ਗ੍ਰਿਹ ਪ੍ਰਿਅ ਥੀਤੇ ਸਦ ਥਾਏ: the soul settled in the Beloved's home (Santhya, the Shabdarth) or the Beloved settled in one's heart-home (the Darpan).
our reading: (one who has) settled for ever in the Beloved's home ever enjoys the joy of love.
alternatives: one in whose home the Beloved has settled for ever enjoys love.
decided because: ਪ੍ਰਿਅ stands as the owner of ਗ੍ਰਿਹ (the Beloved's home); Santhya and the Shabdarth read it so.

issue: ਗਾਰ: filth (Santhya, the Shabdarth) or pride (the Darpan).
our reading: harbour filth in their minds.
alternatives: harbour pride in their minds.
decided because: The Shabdarth notes that ਗਾਰ (mud, filth) is the word here; Santhya reads it so too, and line 5 names the filth (pride, attachment, mine and yours).

issue: ਅਨਿਕ ਤਪੰਥਾ: many austerities (Santhya) or ਅਨਿਕਤ ਪੰਥਾ, many paths (the Darpan, the Shabdarth).
our reading: many have practised austerities.
alternatives: (searching) many paths.
decided because: Our text divides the words ਅਨਿਕ ਤਪੰਥਾ, which gives ਤਪ (austerity).

issue: ਬ੍ਰਹਮ: Brahma (Santhya) or knowers of Brahm (the Darpan).
our reading: Brahma and those like Brahma.
alternatives: the knowers of God, and gods like Brahma.
decided because: In a list of gods and celestials, ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਬ੍ਰਹਮਾਦਿਕ reads most naturally as Brahma and the gods like him.

issue: ਛੁਟਕੀ in its first two uses: the false one's love breaks off, or (Santhya's first reading) when it breaks, release follows.
our reading: the love breaks off, surely breaks off; in the Saakat's company there is no release
alternatives: Santhya: if it breaks there is release; Faridkot: it will break today or tomorrow
decided because: the Darpan's gloss (ਛੁਟਕੀ ਛੁਟਕੀ, surely breaks) fits the subject ਝੂਠੁ ਪਰੀਤਿ, and the third ਛੁਟਕੀ, negated with ਸਾਕਤ ਸੰਗਿ, is then the contrast of release; Faridkot and Santhya's second reading agree

issue: ਤ੍ਰਿਕੁਟੀ: the knitted brow, inner fretting (Darpan), or the three gunas (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa), or doer-deed-act (Faridkot), or the supreme state above three-fold division (Santhya).
our reading: trikuti, the frown of inner fretting
alternatives: the bondage of the three gunas; the triad of doer, deed and act
decided because: the Darpan's word sense (ਤ੍ਰਿ + ਕੁਟੀ, three bent lines of the brow) and the Granth's own rendering at 220.4 (the mind's fretting) agree; consistency with it

issue: Who is described in lines 2 to 4: God (Santhya's first reading: O Bithal, able at all times to show the way, I am a sacrifice to you; you who have no craving, sport in Sahaj, whose place is incomparable) or the Sants (Darpan, Faridkot, Santhya's second reading).
our reading: the Sants: those able at all times to show the path, who sing and are dear to God, who have no craving and delight in Sahaj, whose place is in the One
alternatives: lines 2 and 4 address God himself
decided because: ਉਵਾ ਕੈ (their) in the Rahao needs the Sants as its antecedent, ਕੇ and the verbs are plural, and three of the four readings take the Sants

issue: ਕਰ ਤਲ: the riddhis, siddhis and treasures in God's palms (Darpan) or in the Sants' palms (Faridkot, Santhya).
our reading: in the palms of your (God's) hands
alternatives: in the Sants' palms
decided because: the line goes on in vocatives to God (ਜਗਜੀਵਨ ਸ੍ਰਬ ਨਾਥ ਅਨੇਕੈ ਨਾਉ), so the palms are his

issue: ਟੇਰਤ ਪ੍ਰੇਤਿ ਪੁਕਾਰਿ: they call him a pret (the departed, the dead); Manmohan Singh and Sant Singh Khalsa: a ghost.
our reading: they cry out aloud and call (him) a pret (the dead)
alternatives: a ghost
decided because: the Darpan's gloss (ਗੁਜ਼ਰ ਚੁੱਕਾ) and the Granth's rendering at 134.4 (a pret, the dead)

issue: ਮੇਰਉ ਮੇਰਉ ਸਭੈ ਕਹਤ ਹੈ ਹਿਤ ਸਿਉ ਬਾਧਿਓ ਚੀਤ: everyone says mine, the mind bound by attachment (Darpan, Faridkot), or they say you are mine and bind their minds to you with love (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
our reading: everyone keeps saying mine, mine; the mind is bound by attachment
alternatives: all say you are mine and attach their minds to you
decided because: ਬਾਧਿਓ is a participle with ਚੀਤ as its subject (the mind is bound), and nothing in the line names a you

issue: line 17, ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮਿ ਬਿਗਾਸੇ: Nanak the one who blossoms, or a vocative (ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ without aunkar, and the verb intransitive).
our reading: servant Nanak blossoms through the Name (kept as written).
alternatives: Darpan: O servant Nanak, the one the Guru has shown (the Lord) blossoms through the Name; the same structure at 538.1 line 4 (ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਨਾਮਿ ਸਮਾਏ) is rendered as a vocative in this batch.
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka (the servant blossomed through the Name) and both translations read Nanak as the one who blossoms, and the live meanings already read ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ as the subject of an intransitive verb (206.3 line 10). The line's own grammar does not rule this out, so it is not changed for consistency alone.

issue: line 8, ਹਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਅਰਾਧੇ: a command to the companions (as the review changed it), or a third-person statement.
our reading: a command: come, meet and adore the Name (ਆਓ ... ਮਿਲੋ, ਅਤੇ ... ਅਰਾਧੋ / and adore).
alternatives: The Darpan's word gloss: ਅਰਾਧੇ = ਆਰਾਧਦਾ ਹੈ ((whoever meets the companions) meditates on the Name); the Faridkot Teeka: let us worship.
decided because: The Darpan's own line meaning reads a command (ਸਿਮਰਨ ਕਰੋ). The Faridkot Teeka and both translations read an exhortation. The line is an invitation to the companions, so the -ਏ is read as the rhyme form of the verb that follows ਮਿਲਹੁ.

issue: ਅਨਿਕ ਉਪਰੀਆ: who did what to the many.
our reading: the vices (the evil ones) have laid waste to many (ਉਪਰੀਆ = uprooted, destroyed).
alternatives: Manmohan Singh: I made many efforts (ਉਪਰਾਲੇ) to shake them off.
decided because: Darpan's gloss ਉਪਰੀਆ = ਉਪਾੜਿਆ and the Faridkot Teeka (ਉਖਾੜ ਦੀਆ) agree; the stanza describes the vices, and the Rahao's ਤਉ (that is why) follows from their danger, not from failed efforts.

issue: ਬਿਰਖ ਇਕ ਤਰੀਆ: read as ਇਕਤਰੀਆ (gathered) or ਇਕ ਤਰ (under one tree).
our reading: gathered together under one tree (the world).
alternatives: Darpan: ਇਕਤਰੀਆ, gathered (under the world-tree); the line divides ਇਕ ਤਰੀਆ.
decided because: Both readings give travellers met under a tree; the rendering keeps both the one tree of the printed text and the gathering of the commentaries.

issue: ਚਰਨਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਚਿਤੁ ਲਾਇਓ: statement or exhortation.
our reading: Says Nanak, O mortal: cast off all doubt and fix your mind on his feet (ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ vocative, ਲਾਇਓ the Braj polite imperative).
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, the one who has fixed his mind on his feet has done so only by casting off all doubt (a statement).
decided because: The Faridkot Teeka and both translations read a command; the Ninth Guru's hymns close with counsel to the mortal (ਪ੍ਰਾਣੀ), and -ਇਓ is the Braj respectful imperative.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ ਹਰਿ ਮੇਲਾਇਆ: Nanak vocative or object.
our reading: (The Guru) has united servant Nanak with the Lord.
alternatives: Darpan: O servant Nanak, the one whom the Guru has united with the Lord has many strains playing in the heart.
decided because: ਮੇਲਾਇਆ (caused to meet) wants an object; the stanza moves from the speaker's own longing (my mind is pierced) to his meeting, and the translations read Nanak as the one united.

issue: ਬਿਤਾਲੇ: out of step, or ghouls (ਬੇਤਾਲ).
our reading: out of step (with the true measure of life).
alternatives: Faridkot: ghosts or unsettled; Sant Singh Khalsa: evil demons.
decided because: Darpan's gloss ਤਾਲ ਤੋਂ ਖੁੰਝੇ (without taal) is the grammar-based sense and fits ਮੂੜ (foolish) beside it; the Faridkot Teeka itself gives unsettled as one sense.

issue: ਤਾਰਣਹਾਰੋ: the Guru or the Name carries across.
our reading: the Guru is the one to carry (them) across.
alternatives: Faridkot: the Name, which carries across, the Guru has made firm.
decided because: Darpan reads the Guru; ਤਾਰਣਹਾਰੋ stands in the clause after ਗੁਰਿ ਸਤਿਗੁਰਿ and the Guru as boatman runs through these chhants (538.1 line 14). The sense is the same either way: carried across through the Guru's Name.

issue: ਗਤਿ ਮਿਤਿ ਪਾਇਆ: what is found.
our reading: the high state and the way to it.
alternatives: Darpan: the conduct (ਮਰਯਾਦਾ) of the high spiritual life; Sant Singh Khalsa: the way to salvation; elsewhere ਗਤਿ ਮਿਤਿ is the Lord's state and extent.
decided because: Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ: ਗਤਿ = high spiritual state, ਮਿਤਿ = its measure or rule; with the speaker as the finder, the high state and its way is what the Guru gives.

issue: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ: vocative or subject.
our reading: O servant Nanak, meeting the Guru, (beings) are saved.
alternatives: Servant Nanak, meeting the Guru, is saved.
decided because: ਜਨ ਨਾਨਕ without aunkar is vocative (Darpan), and ਉਬਰੇ, ਸਮਾਣੇ are plural.

issue: ਆਏ ਖਰੇ ਕਠਿਨ ਜਮਕੰਕਰਿ ਪਕੜਿ ਲਇਆ (line 14): one servant of Jam or several (ਆਏ, ਖਰੇ read as plural).
our reading: One: Jam's servant, utterly merciless, has come and seized him (ਜਮਦੂਤ ਨੇ ਆ ਕੇ … ਫੜ ਲਿਆ).
alternatives: Plural: the very merciless servants of Jam came and seized him (the Faridkot Teeka: ਜਮ ਕੰਕਰ ਆਏ … ਜਮਦੂਤੋਂ ਨੇ).
decided because: ਜਮਕੰਕਰਿ is the instrumental singular (the Darpan marks it {ਇਕ-ਵਚਨ}, ਜਮਦੂਤ ਨੇ), with ਖਰੇ as the adverb very; the line goes on in the singular (ਪਕੜੇ ਚਲਾਇਆ, line 15). The sense is the same either way.

issue: ਗੁਰ in ਗੁਰ ਪਾਰਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਪੂਰੇ: the Guru, or great (an epithet of God).
our reading: great: O great and perfect Supreme Lord.
alternatives: O Guru, O perfect Supreme Lord (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh).
decided because: The whole shabad addresses God (ਤੇਰਾ ਭਾਣਾ, ਗੋਪਾਲ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ, ਤੁਝ ਬਿਨਾ); the Darpan and the Faridkot Teeka both read ਗੁਰ as great here, and ਗੁਰ = ਵੱਡਾ is attested (ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਗੁਰ).

issue: ਹਰਿ ਜੀਉ mid-line (lines 8, 13, 14): address or object.
our reading: An address, O dear Lord, in lines 8, 13 and 14; the object or subject in lines 7, 19 and 20, where the sentence needs it.
alternatives: Read as apposition to ਸਚੁ in line 13 (the True One, the dear Lord).
decided because: The commentaries all read it as a vocative in 8, 13 and 14; it is the chhant's filler address, like ਮੇਰੀ ਜਿੰਦੁੜੀਏ in the shabads before.

issue: ਸੰਤ ਜੰਪੈ ਜਿਨਿ … ਮਿਲਾਇਆ: what ਜੰਪੈ means and who has united whom.
our reading: Nanak makes his plea and speaks to the Sant (the Guru) who has united him with the Lord through the destined union.
alternatives: Nanak meditates on the Sant who … (Faridkot, Sant Singh Khalsa); the Darpan: pleads before the Guru, who has united me.
decided because: ਜੰਪੈ is to utter, speak; line 6 (ਸੰਤ ਜੰਪੈ ਮੇਲਿ ਕੰਤੁ) shows it as speaking to the Sant, and both lines are rendered alike.

issue: ਅਨ ਕਾਏ: two words (why … in another) or one (ਅਨਕਾਏ, in trivial things).
our reading: Why are you steeped in what is other (than God)?
alternatives: The Darpan: ਅਨਕਾਏ, in trivial things (O you steeped in trivial things, your road is painful).
decided because: The text as printed separates ਅਨ ਕਾਏ; ਕਾਏ is the Braj why (kāhe) and ਅਨ other; the Faridkot Teeka and the translations read it so.

issue: ਤਜਿ ਨ ਜਾਈ: the refuge he does not leave, or God who does not leave him.
our reading: He has found the Lord's refuge and does not forsake it to go elsewhere.
alternatives: The Darpan: the refuge of God, who never leaves (him).
decided because: The subject of ਪਾਈ and ਜਾਈ is most simply the same person; Faridkot and Manmohan Singh read it so.

issue: ਸੰਜੋਗਿ ਭੂਲਾ: by destiny, or by association (with lust and the rest).
our reading: by the lot written for him he went astray.
alternatives: The Darpan: because of his union with lust, anger and the rest.
decided because: ਸੰਜੋਗ in Gurbani most often is what is ordained; the line follows the writ of line 12 (ਲੇਖੁ ਲਿਖਿਆ); Faridkot reads by the conjunction of evil deeds, which is the same writ.

issue: ਨ ਬੀਸਰੈ: a statement or a wish.
