our reading: A wish: may the Lord never slip from the mind.
alternatives: A statement: (he) is not forgotten from the mind (of those who repeat the Name), as the Darpan reads.
decided because: The line stands between commands to the listener (ਪੀਉ, line 13); the optative fits the prayer of line 22 (ਹਰਿ ਬਿਸਰੁ ਨਾਹੀ).

issue: ਨਹ ਕਾਂਮ ਪੂਰਨ ਗਿਆਨੇ (line 17): ਕਾਂਮ as desires or as life's purpose.
our reading: nor are desires fulfilled, nor does wisdom come (kept).
alternatives: Darpan: ਕਾਂਮ = the purpose of human birth (ਮਨੁੱਖਾ ਜਨਮ ਦਾ ਮਨੋਰਥ), not attained.
decided because: ਕਾਂਮ bears 'desires' in the plain sense and the line pairs it with ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨ; the reading is not wrong, so not changed for taste.

issue: English title of the vaar: the Gurmukhi has the oblique ਬਿਹਾਗੜੇ; the part is named Raag Bihagra.
our reading: Bihagre ki Vaar
alternatives: Bihagra ki Vaar; Raag Bihagra ki Vaar
decided because: A name follows its Gurmukhi spelling (as Gauri ki Vaar, Sri Raag ki Vaar keep the title's own form); the Darpan and Santhya name it ਬਿਹਾਗੜੇ ਕੀ ਵਾਰ. The merger should keep one form for the title wherever it appears.

issue: ਨਰਪਤਿ ਜਾਣਿ ਗ੍ਰਹਿਓ ਸੇਵਕ ਸਿਆਣੇ: who is ਨਰਪਤਿ and what is ਗ੍ਰਹਿਓ.
our reading: O king, you are held fast, taking (these) clever servants to be your own (ਨਰਪਤਿ vocative, ਗ੍ਰਹਿਓ a participle, caught).
alternatives: Darpan: a king (subject), taking wise servants as his own, is caught; Faridkot and Manmohan Singh: ਗ੍ਰਹਿਓ as ਗ੍ਰਿਹ, the house (O king, the house you think yours and your clever servants); Santhya: O king, know that (these) wise servants must part.
decided because: The chhant addresses the king throughout (ਰਾਜਨ in the stanza before); ਗ੍ਰਹਿਓ has the participle's -ਓ ending; the Darpan's gloss of the verb is kept with the vocative of the Faridkot Teeka and Santhya.

issue: Who is addressed in the fourth stanza (lines 19 to 23).
our reading: The king, as in the stanzas before: (the Lord) has made you his own, pulled you out, given you the Saadh's company; your tongue worships, your mind and body are soaked.
alternatives: Darpan: a general statement (whom God makes his own, he pulls out …; whoever worships with the tongue …).
decided because: ਸੰਗਿ ਤੇਰੈ ਸੇ ਚਲੇ (line 22) addresses a 'you'; the Faridkot Teeka and Santhya read the stanza as the Guru's word to the king, and the chhant's address is kept.

issue: ਤੂ ਨੇਤ੍ਰੀ ਦੇਖਿ ਚਲਿਆ ਮਾਇਆ ਬਿਉਹਾਰੀ.
our reading: You have seen with your own eyes that the dealer in Maya departs (leaving it all).
alternatives: Faridkot: you, having seen Maya's dealings with your eyes, are departing; Darpan: look with your eyes: the one who deals only in Maya departs.
decided because: Santhya's reading (you have seen with your eyes that Maya goes with no one) fits ਤੂ as the one who has seen, and the next line (nothing goes with you).

issue: ਜਹ ਭਾਵਤ ਤਹ ਜਾਹੀ: whose pleasure.
our reading: they go where (the Lord) wills.
alternatives: Santhya: they reach wherever they wish (but not their true home).
decided because: The Darpan's reading; the next line names the all-pervading Lord, and the stanza's point is that cleverness fails.

issue: ਸਹਜੇ ਹੋਇ ਸੁ ਹੋਇ.
our reading: whatever happens comes about in Sahaj.
alternatives: Darpan: whatever happens is seen to happen in God's will; Faridkot: let happen what happens of itself (he is beyond joy and grief).
decided because: The plain words, which bear both readings; Sahaj is kept as the term.

issue: ਜਿਨਿ: the tongue or the person.
our reading: the tongue which has enshrined the Lord in the mind (ਜਿਨਿ = the tongue).
alternatives: Manmohan Singh, Faridkot: the tongue of one who has enshrined the Lord in his mind.
decided because: Line 1 has the same ਸਾ ਰਸਨਾ … ਜਿਨਿ, where ਜਿਨਿ is the tongue; the Darpan reads both lines so.

issue: The image of the tree, the one fruit and the two birds.
our reading: The literal image in the meaning (the fruit as the Lord's essence, as line 4 names it), with both readings in a note.
alternatives: Darpan: world-tree, fruit = attachment to Maya, birds = Gurmukh and manmukh; Santhya: tree = body, fruit = Hari-ras, birds = soul and Supreme Soul (Rig Veda 1.164.20, Mundaka Upanishad).
decided because: The lines give the image only; line 4 itself calls the fruit ਹਰਿ ਰਸਿ ਫਲਿ, so the fruit is not rendered as Maya; one note tells the two traditions.

issue: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਜੀਅ ਪ੍ਰਾਨ ਅਧਾਰੀ: vocative or appositive.
our reading: Nanak prays: I am the servant of the Lord God, the support of soul and breath.
alternatives: Faridkot: O God, support of soul and breath, I am your servant.
decided because: The Darpan's reading; the sense is the same either way.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ ਦਰਸਨੁ ਪੇਖਿ ਜੀਵੇ: who lives.
our reading: Nanak lives by beholding (his) sight.
alternatives: Darpan: O Nanak, those who sing … live by the sight.
decided because: Nanak speaks of himself (style §12); the Faridkot Teeka and the first-person stanza (I was parted, I sang) bear it out.

issue: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਸਿਰਿ ਕਰਤਾਰੁ: two or one.
our reading: the True Guru and the Creator over their heads.
alternatives: Faridkot, Manmohan Singh: the True Guru who is the Creator.
decided because: The Darpan's reading; the words list both and the meaning does not decide between them beyond the line.

issue: ਅਲਿਪਤ ਬੰਧਨ ਰਹਤ ਕਰਤਾ: statement or vocative.
our reading: The Creator is untouched and free of bonds; (we) reap what we ourselves have done.
alternatives: Faridkot: O untouched Creator, free of bonds!
decided because: The Darpan's reading; the verb-less clause reads as a statement set against the next half.

issue: ਜਨੁ ਨਾਨਕ (ਨਾਨਕ without aunkar): vocative or subject?
our reading: Servant Nanak tells the greatness of the Lord
alternatives: O Nanak, (a rare) servant tells his greatness (the Darpan's full text)
decided because: The Sahib Singh line in the refs, the Faridkot (ਮੈਂ … ਕਹਿਤਾ ਹੂੰ) and both English read Nanak the speaker; ਜਨੁ ਨਾਨਕ in a pauri's close is the Guru's signature, as 552.4 (ਜਨੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ) renders it.

issue: ਮਾਣਸੁ ਭਰਿਆ ਆਣਿਆ ਮਾਣਸੁ ਭਰਿਆ ਆਇ
our reading: one brings a vessel filled (with wine), another comes and fills (his cup)
alternatives: a man brought (into the world) soiled comes and is soiled further (the Darpan's full text)
decided because: The wine image runs through the whole salok (ਜਿਤੁ ਪੀਤੈ twice, ਝੂਠਾ ਮਦੁ, ਸਚੁ ਮਦੁ); the Sahib Singh line in the refs and the Faridkot read the vessel and the cup.

issue: ਰਜਾਇ: whose will — God's or the True Guru's?
our reading: by (God's) will the True Guru meets the blind
alternatives: in the True Guru's will (Faridkot; Manmohan Singh: if he blends with the Guru's will)
decided because: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ (aunkar) is the subject of ਮਿਲੈ, so the Guru meets him; the Darpan reads ਰਜਾਇ as the Lord's will, which fits a meeting granted, not achieved.

issue: Who is in the Creator's refuge: Nanak or the enlightened person?
our reading: O Nanak, (he stays) in the Creator's refuge, and the Creator keeps his honour
alternatives: Nanak seeks the Creator's refuge (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: The salok speaks of the blind man who meets the Guru (lines 1-3); ਰਾਖੈ is third person; the Darpan reads the same; style.md §12: a line telling of someone else takes O Nanak.

issue: ਅਰਧਿ ਉਰਧਿ
our reading: (him who pervades) below and above, kept in their hearts
alternatives: in this world and the next (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa)
decided because: Darpan and Faridkot both read the Lord pervading below and above (patal and sky); our earlier renderings of ਅਰਧ ਉਰਧ (228.1, 333.2, 344.4) take below/above.

issue: ਅਨਦਿਨੁ ਰਹੈ ਸਦਾ ਗੁਣ ਗਾਇ: concessive or positive?
our reading: God is not found by saying and describing, even if one sings his virtues night and day
alternatives: not found by talk; the one who sings his virtues night and day finds him (Faridkot)
decided because: Line 2 (without grace none has found him) and line 4 (found through his glance of grace) carry the salok; the Darpan reads it concessively.

issue: ਨਾਨਕ with a command to the Sheikh (ਪੁਛਹੁ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਜਾਇ)
our reading: Says Nanak: … go and ask any man of wisdom
alternatives: O Nanak (Darpan)
decided because: style.md §12: Nanak tells the listener something with a command, so Says Nanak; O Nanak would make Nanak the one told to go and ask.

issue: ਸਤਿਗੁਰੁ ਪਾਇਆ ਕਰਮਿ ਪਰਾਪਤਿ ਹੋਇ: what is attained, and is Nanak the finder?
our reading: O Nanak, when the True Guru is found, (the Naam) is attained by (God's) grace
alternatives: Nanak has found the True Guru; by his grace the Name is obtained (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh); the Guru is obtained by past merit (Faridkot)
decided because: The salok is about the Naam (lines 1-3); the Darpan reads Nanak as vocative and the Naam as what is attained, meeting the Guru as the means.

issue: ਆਪੇ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਭੰਜਨੁ
our reading: he himself, through the Guru, breaks (the bonds of Maya)
alternatives: he breaks the bonds of the Gurmukhs (Sant Singh Khalsa); becoming Gurmukh he does bhajan / destroys the Gurmukhs' pains (Faridkot)
decided because: ਭੰਜਨੁ is a breaker (Darpan: ਨਾਸ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲਾ), parallel to ਪਾਪ ਖੰਡਨੁ in line 2; ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ as adverb by our settled rendering.

issue: ਸਲੋਕੁ ਮਰਦਾਨਾ ੧: author or addressee?
our reading: Salok, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji), addressed to Mardana
alternatives: Salok of Mardana (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh)
decided because: The ੧ and the signature Nanak in each salok mark the First Guru; the Darpan says so and the Faridkot has the Guru speaking to Mardana; one note says it.

issue: ਤੰਤੁ, ਪਰਮ ਤੰਤੁ
our reading: the thread (the soul) and the supreme thread (God)
alternatives: element and supreme essence
decided because: Darpan (small string and great string) and Faridkot (jiva and Ishvar) agree; the line pairs the two as Master and servant are paired after it.

issue: ਸੋ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਸਿਮਰੀਐ ਤਿਸੁ ਦੇਹੀ ਕਉ ਪਾਲਿ
our reading: (the body through which) that God is remembered: cherish that body
alternatives: remember the God who has nourished the body (the refs' Darpan line)
decided because: ਪਾਲਿ is an imperative (no ਜਿਨਿ for who nourished); the Darpan's own full text and the Faridkot read: cherish the body in which God is remembered, answering the cursed body of the salok before.

issue: ਸੋ ਸਚਾ ਹਰਿ ਜਾਨੁ
our reading: that servant of the Lord is (one with) the True One
alternatives: comes to know the True Lord (Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh); know that one to be true (Faridkot)
decided because: Darpan's ਪਦਅਰਥ: ਹਰਿ ਜਾਨੁ = ਹਰਿ ਜਨੁ, ਸਚਾ = (the form of) God; the pauri ends on the servant whose honour is kept.

issue: Subject of ਰਖਸੀ and the form of ਨਾਨਕ
our reading: Says Nanak: (this medicine) will keep you in peace here
alternatives: the Guru will keep you; O Nanak
decided because: The salok is a prescription (ਦਾਰੂ, ਸੰਜਮੁ); the Darpan and Faridkot take the medicine as subject; the line promises the listeners (ਕਰੇਹੁ), so Says Nanak (style.md §12).

review: The doubt's decision rests on a wrong premise (that ਖਾਹੁ can only be the second person plural imperative); decide it the other way.

issue: Which comes first: understanding or dying while living.
our reading: When understanding comes to the world, it dies while living (understanding brings the dying to self).
alternatives: Faridkot: when one dies to the self, then understanding comes.
decided because: ਜਾ … ਹੋਇ is the when-clause, so understanding is the condition; the Darpan and the Santhya read it so, and line 2 (God wakes it, then awareness comes) puts understanding first.

issue: ਤੇਰੀ is feminine while ਵਖਰੁ, ਨਾਮੁ, ਧਨੁ are masculine.
our reading: the cargo, the wealth of your Name, O Lord (ਹਰਿ vocative, ਤੇਰੀ read with the Name as the Darpan and the Shabdarth do).
alternatives: Santhya lists readings: ਧਨੁ as dhanya, worthy merchandise (Faridkot); or ਤੇਰੀ with an implied ਭਗਤੀ, your devotion.
decided because: The sense your Name as the wealth and cargo is shared by all readings and needs no word added; the Darpan and Shabdarth gloss it so.

issue: ਹਾਣਤ: shame or harm/loss.
our reading: never any harm (ਹਾਨੀ).
alternatives: Darpan: ਸ਼ਰਮਿੰਦਗੀ, shame (in the Lord's court); Sant Singh Khalsa, Manmohan Singh: humiliation.
decided because: Santhya (from Skt hāni), the Shabdarth (ਹਾਣ, ਨੁਕਸਾਨ, ਘਾਟਾ) and Faridkot (ਨਾਸੁ) read loss or harm, which fits the wealth image of the salok; harm covers both sides.

issue: ਗਉਹਰੁ: the deep ocean, or a pearl/essence (Persian gauhar).
our reading: the fathomless ocean.
alternatives: Faridkot: ਮੋਤੀ, pearl; Platts: gauhar, essence, pearl; Santhya: the reality of all things; our 101.3 renders ਗਉਹਰੁ there as pearl.
decided because: The Darpan and the Shabdarth (ਗੰਭੀਰ, ਡੂੰਘਾ ਸਮੁੰਦਰ) read deep ocean, and it pairs with knowing his own measure (ਮਿਤਿ); at 101.3 ਗਹਿਰ ਗਭੀਰਾ already says deep, so pearl stays there.

issue: Tense of ਬੈਠਾ ਤਾੜੀ ਲਾਇ: before creation (past) or now, apart from his creation (present).
our reading: past: he sat in deep absorption, apart from all.
alternatives: Darpan: present, having made the creation he still sits apart from it.
decided because: Lines 3 and 4 tell of the time before creation (ਵਰਤਿਆ, ਓਥੈ … ਨ); Santhya and Faridkot read line 5 in that time.

issue: ਨ ਚੇਤਈ ਕਿ ਕਰੇਗੁ ਅਗੈ ਜਾਇ: does not remember (God), what will it do hereafter; or does not consider what it will do hereafter.
our reading: it does not remember (the Lord); what will it do when it goes on ahead?
alternatives: does not stop to think what it will do on going ahead.
decided because: ਚੇਤਣਾ in Gurbani is remembering the Lord (as in 556.1 ਚੇਤਿਆ ਨ ਜਾਇ); the Darpan, Faridkot and both English refs read it so.

issue: ਆਪੇ ਲਾਇ ਧਿਆਨਾਂ: he himself meditates, or he himself joins others to meditation.
our reading: he himself becomes absorbed in meditation.
alternatives: he himself enjoins (us) to meditation (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa).
decided because: The pauri is a list of roles God himself plays (the Knower, the silent sage, the speaker of knowledge); the Darpan reads ਆਪ ਹੀ ਬਿਰਤੀ ਜੋੜਦਾ ਹੈ, and no object is in the line.

issue: ਮੂਲੇ ਭੂਲੇ: utterly astray, or forgetful of the Primal (Mool) Lord.
our reading: utterly gone astray.
alternatives: have forgotten the Primal Lord (Manmohan Singh, Sant Singh Khalsa; Faridkot).
decided because: ਮੂਲੇ is the adverb ਮੂਲਿ/ਮੂਲੇ, at all, utterly, as the Darpan and the Santhya read it; ਅਖੁਟੀ ਜਾਂਹੀ, going on a wrong path (Santhya: Skt a-khuṭi), completes it.

issue: ਰਜਿ ਰਜਿ ਜਨ ਖਾਹੁ: a statement (the servants eat their fill) or a command.
our reading: a command: eat your fill of it, O servants (of the Lord).
alternatives: Darpan, Faridkot and the English refs: the servants eat it to their fill.
decided because: ਖਾਹੁ is the second person plural imperative (the third person would be ਖਾਹਿ), and ਜਨ stands as the address; a command stays a command.

issue: ਸਭੁ ਕੋ ਵਸੈ: who or what dwells in the yogi's town.
our reading: all (the virtues) dwell in the town of his body.
alternatives: everyone (all people) dwells in his town, i.e. the world is his home.
decided because: The Darpan, the Santhya and Faridkot all read the town as the body and all as every virtue; the implied word is in brackets.
